एअर इंडिया ने पहले बताया था कि सभी यात्री और क्रू सुरक्षित हैं। किसी के गंभीर रूप से घायल होने की खबर नहीं है। घटना की जांच की जा रही है। टर्बुलेंस के बाद फ्लाइट की तस्वीरें सामने आई हैं, जिनमें प्लेन की सीलिंग के पैनल में दरारें दिखीं।
विमान की छत में दरारें…2 तस्वीरें…
आंख-गर्दन में चोटें, घायलों की 3 तस्वीरें
टर्बुलेंस में अचानक कई फीट नीचे आ सकता है विमान
टर्बुलेंस का मतलब है हवा का बहाव अचानक बदल जाना, जिससे विमान को झटके लगने लगते हैं। इस दौरान विमान कुछ समय के लिए ऊपर-नीचे या दाएं-बाएं हिल सकता है और कभी-कभी कुछ फीट नीचे भी आ जाता है। इसी वजह से यात्रियों को लगता है कि विमान गिर रहा है। हालांकि, ज्यादातर मामलों में ऐसा नहीं होता।
टर्बुलेंस तीव्रता के लिहाज से तीन तरह के होते हैं
- हल्के टर्बुलेंस: इसमें प्लेन 1 मीटर तक ऊपर-नीचे होता है। यात्रियों को पता भी नहीं चलता।
- मध्यम टर्बुलेंस: इसमें जहाज 3-6 मीटर तक ऊपर-नीचे होते हैं। इससे ड्रिंक गिर सकता है।
- गंभीर टर्बुलेंस: इसमें जहाज 30 मीटर तक ऊपर-नीचे होते हैं। सीट बेल्ट न लगाए रहने पर पैसेंजर उछलकर गिर सकते हैं।
क्या टर्बुलेंस की वजह से प्लेन क्रैश हो सकता है?
आधुनिक तकनीक और बेहतर सुरक्षा सिस्टम की वजह से आज टर्बुलेंस से विमान हादसे की आशंका काफी कम हो गई है। हालांकि, बेहद गंभीर टर्बुलेंस या खराब मौसम में दुर्घटना का खतरा पूरी तरह खत्म नहीं होता।
हालांकि, आज के आधुनिक विमान हर तरह के टर्बुलेंस को झेलने के हिसाब से बनाए जाते हैं। पायलटों को भी ऐसी परिस्थितियों से सुरक्षित तरीके से निपटने की विशेष ट्रेनिंग दी जाती है।
दुनिया में टर्बुलेंस से जुड़े 3 बड़े विमान हादसे
- 1994 में अमेरिका की यूएस एयर फ्लाइट 1016 लैंडिंग के दौरान तूफान से पैदा हुए टर्बुलेंस की चपेट में आकर क्रैश हो गई थी। इस हादसे में 37 लोगों की मौत हुई थी।
- 1999 में अमेरिकन एयरलाइंस फ्लाइट 1420 भी खराब मौसम और टर्बुलेंस के बाद रनवे से फिसलकर क्रैश हो गई थी, जिसमें 11 लोगों की जान गई।
- 2001 में अमेरिकन एयरलाइंस फ्लाइट 587 टेकऑफ के कुछ देर बाद वेक टर्बुलेंस की वजह से क्रैश हो गई थी। इस हादसे में विमान में सवार सभी 260 लोगों की मौत हो गई थी।

deduped_items.title: One week on, disaster response in Kumamoto shifts to helping survivors
deduped_items.summary: Uneven conditions at evacuation centers, where summer heat is compounding shortages of water and other essentials, are raising fears of heatstroke and blood clots among survivors.
deduped_items.body_text:
A week after a devastating earthquake registering shindo 7, the highest level on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, struck Kumamoto Prefecture, the disaster response is shifting from search and rescue to stabilizing survivors’ lives and preventing disaster-related casualties.
But uneven conditions across evacuation centers, where shortages of water and other essentials have been compounded by scorching summer heat, are raising fears of heatstroke and blood clots, medical experts said.
The latest prefectural tally shows the death toll from the July 28 earthquake remained at 38 as of Tuesday afternoon, while 123 had been injured. One is suspected to have suffered from heatstroke while taking refuge inside a car as temperatures in the region soared.

deduped_items.title: ANA機と国の飛行検査機、羽田上空で「ニアミス」 防止装置が作動
deduped_items.body_text:
ANA機と国の飛行検査機、羽田上空で「ニアミス」 防止装置が作動
羽田空港近くの上空で4日午前5時44分ごろ、着陸しようと接近していた全日本空輸（ANA）機と、「ドクターホワイト」と呼ばれる国の飛行検査機が「異常接近（ニアミス）」する事案があった。航空機同士の衝突の危険性を知らせる「空中衝突防止装置」（TCAS）が作動したため衝突は回避。ANAが事態を国土交通省に報告した。
ANAや国交省によると、着陸しようとしていたのは上海発羽田行きのNH968便（乗員・乗客197人）で、当初の計画では4日午前5時45分に到着予定だった。C滑走路に向けて降下中にTCASが作動してアラートが鳴り、着陸を中止して上昇し、衝突を回避した。最終的には午前6時10分に着陸し、乗員・乗客にけが人などはいないという。
国交省によると、検査機はD滑走路から離陸した後に旋回し、ANA機が着陸しようと降下している経路を横切るように飛んでいた。検査機にはTCASから避難指示は出ていないといい、詳しく調べている。
検査機は国交省が運用し、航空機の安全な飛行に欠かせない無線施設や灯火などが、正常に作動しているかを上空から確認する。無線やレーダー施設などが機能しているかを実際に飛んで調べており、国が「ドクターホワイト」としてPRしている。
早朝の羽田の上空では何が起…

中部電、社員などの情報7万4千件流出か 不審な連絡に注意呼びかけ
中部電力は4日、外部から不正アクセスを受けて取引先や社員など約7万4千人の個人情報が流出した恐れがあると発表した。悪用された被害は確認されておらず、システム障害や電力供給への影響もないという。
中部電によると、7月29日に第三者機関からの情報提供で発覚した。役職員の約2400件のメールや連絡先情報が不正に閲覧された可能性があり、取引先や中部電の役職員などの役職や氏名、メールアドレス、電話番号が流出した恐れがあるという。中部電は、従業員を装った不審なメールや電話への注意を呼びかけている。

deduped_items.body_text:
車7台に衝突し6人にけがさせたか、男逮捕 ベントレー乗り捨て逃走
松田果穂
東京都八王子市で3月、高級外車「ベントレー」を運転して信号待ちの車7台に次々と衝突して計6人にけがをさせたとして、警視庁は、韓国籍の住所不定、無職の男（49）を自動車運転死傷処罰法違反（過失運転致傷）や傷害などの疑いで再逮捕し、4日に発表した。容疑を認めているという。
交通捜査課によると、逮捕容疑は3月23日午前7時半ごろ、八王子市の片側2車線の国道を直進中、赤信号で停車中の車列の間を抜けようとして乗用車など計7台に衝突し、車内にいた男女6人にけがを負わせるなどしたというもの。
男の車は、車列の最後尾付近にいた車3台に衝突して3人にけがを負わせた後、さらに加速して車列の中央を進み、別の車4台に衝突して3人にけがを負わせたとみられるという。
警視庁は、男がけがをさせる可能性を認識しながら加速して衝突したとして、傷害容疑にもあたると判断したという。

deduped_items.title: 高木美帆さんに国民栄誉賞授与 冬季五輪でメダル通算10個
deduped_items.body_text:
日本女子最多の五輪メダル通算10個を獲得したスピードスケートの高木美帆さん（32）が4日、首相官邸で国民栄誉賞を授与された。2023年の車いすテニス男子の国枝慎吾さん以来で、29例目となり、高市早苗首相から表彰状を受け取った。
北海道出身の高木さんは、15歳で10年バンクーバー五輪に出場し「スーパー中学生」として話題となった。18年平昌大会で団体追い抜きの金などメダル3個、22年北京大会で1000メートル金など4個を獲得。4度目だった今年2月のミラノ・コルティナ大会は銅3個を手にし、現役を引退した。
国民栄誉賞は1977年創設で、スポーツや芸能、文化などの分野で功績を上げた個人、団体をたたえる。（共同）

deduped_items.title: Mianmar divulga fotos de ex-líder presa há cinco anos em meio a preocupações com sua saúde
deduped_items.summary: O governo de Mianmar, apoiado pelos militares, divulgou fotos da ex-líder Aung San Suu Kyi em uma medida rara, em meio a crescentes preocupações com a saúde da laureada com o Nobel da Paz que está presa. O Gabinete de Imprensa e Informação da Presidência de Mianmar divulgou na segunda-feira duas fotos de Aung San Suu Kyi em encontro com Arnaud de Baecque, representante residente do Comitê Internacional da Cruz Vermelha. Acredita-se que este seja seu primeiro encontro com um enviado estrangeiro d

deduped_items.title: 'Não houve explicação sobre o que fazer se o barco virasse': familiares apontam falhas após acidente nas Cataratas
deduped_items.summary: 'Acabamos todos debaixo do barco': o que dizem os depoimentos dos sobreviventes do acidente nas Cataratas do Iguaçu Os sobreviventes do acidente com uma embarcação nas Cataratas do Iguaçu, que matou o turista holandês Mark Lessink, de 25 anos, afirmaram à Polícia Civil que não receberam orientações sobre como agir em caso de emergência antes do início do passeio. deduped_items.body_text:
Os sobreviventes do acidente com uma embarcação nas Cataratas do Iguaçu, que matou o turista holandês Mark Lessink, de 25 anos, afirmaram à Polícia Civil que não receberam orientações sobre como agir em caso de emergência antes do início do passeio.
Os depoimentos, obtidos com exclusividade pelo Fantástico, fazem parte da investigação que apura as circunstâncias do tombamento da embarcação, ocorrido na última terça-feira (28). Além da dinâmica do acidente, a polícia também investiga se os protocolos de segurança adotados pela empresa responsável eram suficientes.
Segundo um dos sobreviventes, a família recebeu os coletes salva-vidas antes do embarque, mas nenhuma explicação sobre o uso correto do equipamento ou sobre os procedimentos em caso de capotamento da embarcação.
"Ao chegarmos ao barco, recebemos coletes salva-vidas que precisávamos prender na altura da cintura. Não houve nenhuma explicação sobre o uso do colete ou sobre o que fazer caso o barco virasse", afirmou em depoimento.
A falta de orientações também foi mencionada por uma testemunha. Karen Charlotte viajava com a família.
"Não há uma orientação se caso acontecer alguma coisa. A gente não foi orientado antes. Se você cair na água, se acontecer algo, deita de costas ou coisa assim. Nada disso."
Coletes também foram alvo de críticas
Além da ausência de instruções, os sobreviventes relataram dificuldades para permanecer na superfície após o barco virar.
Segundo o depoimento, o modelo de colete utilizado prendia apenas na cintura, o que fazia o equipamento subir durante a tentativa de flutuação.
"Havia uma fita que prendia na cintura, mas como não prendia por baixo, entre as pernas, o colete sempre subia."
De acordo com o advogado que acompanha a família, os sobreviventes enfrentaram dificuldades para se manter na superfície porque as correntes do Rio Iguaçu eram fortes.
"Eles tiveram extrema dificuldade de permanecer em cima da água. As correntinhas levavam para baixo e o colete não era suficiente para mantê-los em cima da água", afirmou.
'Não houve explicação sobre o que fazer se o barco virasse': sobreviventes apontam falhas em passeio nas Cataratas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo
Investigação apura possíveis falhas
A Polícia Civil informou que, até o momento, não encontrou indícios de irregularidades na atuação dos dois pilotos da embarcação.
As investigações, porém, passaram a analisar se houve falhas nos protocolos de segurança adotados antes do passeio.
Segundo o delegado responsável pelo caso, os depoimentos indicam que pode ter havido deficiência nas orientações repassadas aos turistas.
"Nós notamos, pelos relatos das testemunhas, uma falta de protocolos de segurança, orientação sobre o que fazer quando a embarcação vira, sobre como colocar o colete e também como verificar se ele está em condições de uso", afirmou.
O laudo da Polícia Científica concluiu que Mark Lessink morreu por afogamento. A investigação agora busca identificar se gestores da operação podem ser responsabilizados por homicídio culposo.

deduped_items.body_text:
A Polícia Civil do RJ iniciou nesta terça-feira (4) a Operação Quimera, que mira a exploração de clubes recreativos para lavar dinheiro do Comando Vermelho (CV).
Agentes da 52ª DP (Nova Iguaçu) saíram para cumprir mandados de busca e apreensão em 10 endereços — um deles é o Várzea Country Clube, em Água Santa, na Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro.
O esquema, que movimentou R$ 11 milhões, incluiu ainda uma pousada em Armação dos Búzios, na Região dos Lagos, e extorsões a outros clubes recreativos.
Segundo as investigações, traficantes do Morro do Dezoito colocaram pessoas de confiança para administrar o Várzea Country Clube, que seguiu promovendo festas e eventos.
Esta reportagem está em atualização.
Várzea Country Clube fica em Água Santa — Foto: Divulgação/PCERJ

deduped_items.body_text:
Os sobreviventes do acidente com uma embarcação nas Cataratas do Iguaçu, que matou o turista holandês Mark Lessink, de 25 anos, afirmaram à Polícia Civil que não receberam orientações sobre como agir em caso de emergência antes do início do passeio.
Os depoimentos, obtidos com exclusividade pelo Fantástico, fazem parte da investigação que apura as circunstâncias do tombamento da embarcação, ocorrido na última terça-feira (28). Além da dinâmica do acidente, a polícia também investiga se os protocolos de segurança adotados pela empresa responsável eram suficientes.
Segundo um dos sobreviventes, a família recebeu os coletes salva-vidas antes do embarque, mas nenhuma explicação sobre o uso correto do equipamento ou sobre os procedimentos em caso de capotamento da embarcação.
"Ao chegarmos ao barco, recebemos coletes salva-vidas que precisávamos prender na altura da cintura. Não houve nenhuma explicação sobre o uso do colete ou sobre o que fazer caso o barco virasse", afirmou em depoimento.
A falta de orientações também foi mencionada por uma testemunha. Karen Charlotte viajava com a família.
"Não há uma orientação se caso acontecer alguma coisa. A gente não foi orientado antes. Se você cair na água, se acontecer algo, deita de costas ou coisa assim. Nada disso."
Coletes também foram alvo de críticas
Além da ausência de instruções, os sobreviventes relataram dificuldades para permanecer na superfície após o barco virar.
Segundo o depoimento, o modelo de colete utilizado prendia apenas na cintura, o que fazia o equipamento subir durante a tentativa de flutuação.
"Havia uma fita que prendia na cintura, mas como não prendia por baixo, entre as pernas, o colete sempre subia."
De acordo com o advogado que acompanha a família, os sobreviventes enfrentaram dificuldades para se manter na superfície porque as correntes do Rio Iguaçu eram fortes.
"Eles tiveram extrema dificuldade de permanecer em cima da água. As correntinhas levavam para baixo e o colete não era suficiente para mantê-los em cima da água", afirmou.
'Não houve explicação sobre o que fazer se o barco virasse': sobreviventes apontam falhas em passeio nas Cataratas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo
Investigação apura possíveis falhas
A Polícia Civil informou que, até o momento, não encontrou indícios de irregularidades na atuação dos dois pilotos da embarcação.
As investigações, porém, passaram a analisar se houve falhas nos protocolos de segurança adotados antes do passeio.
Segundo o delegado responsável pelo caso, os depoimentos indicam que pode ter havido deficiência nas orientações repassadas aos turistas.
"Nós notamos, pelos relatos das testemunhas, uma falta de protocolos de segurança, orientação sobre o que fazer quando a embarcação vira, sobre como colocar o colete e também como verificar se ele está em condições de uso", afirmou.
O laudo da Polícia Científica concluiu que Mark Lessink morreu por afogamento. A investigação agora busca identificar se gestores da operação podem ser responsabilizados por homicídio culposo.
Empresa nega falhas
A empresa responsável pelo passeio informou que realizou, nesta semana, uma reciclagem com todos os funcionários sobre os procedimentos de segurança. Segundo a empresa, as certificações obtidas indicam que não há necessidade de mudanças e, por isso, os protocolos permanecem os mesmos.
A empresa também contestou o relato da família holandesa de que não houve orientações antes do passeio. De acordo com a concessionária, os turistas recebem instruções de segurança em diferentes etapas da experiência.
"Existe um primeiro briefing na carretinha, outro na trilha suspensa e, além disso, toda uma comunicação visual por meio de placas informativas em três idiomas. Antes de iniciar o passeio, é realizado mais um briefing de segurança com orientações específicas sobre a embarcação", informou o gerente administrativo da empresa, Paulo Ricardo de Cordova.
A empresa também rebateu as críticas feitas pelos sobreviventes ao modelo de colete salva-vidas util
deduped_items.normalised_title: não houve explicação sobre o que fazer se o barco virasse familiares apontam falhas após acidente nas cataratas

deduped_items.body_text:
Os sobreviventes do acidente com uma embarcação nas Cataratas do Iguaçu, que matou o turista holandês Mark Lessink, de 25 anos, afirmaram à Polícia Civil que não receberam orientações sobre como agir em caso de emergência antes do início do passeio.
Os depoimentos, obtidos com exclusividade pelo Fantástico, fazem parte da investigação que apura as circunstâncias do tombamento da embarcação, ocorrido na última terça-feira (28). Além da dinâmica do acidente, a polícia também investiga se os protocolos de segurança adotados pela empresa responsável eram suficientes.
Segundo um dos sobreviventes, a família recebeu os coletes salva-vidas antes do embarque, mas nenhuma explicação sobre o uso correto do equipamento ou sobre os procedimentos em caso de capotamento da embarcação.
"Ao chegarmos ao barco, recebemos coletes salva-vidas que precisávamos prender na altura da cintura. Não houve nenhuma explicação sobre o uso do colete ou sobre o que fazer caso o barco virasse", afirmou em depoimento.
A falta de orientações também foi mencionada por uma testemunha. Karen Charlotte viajava com a família.
"Não há uma orientação se caso acontecer alguma coisa. A gente não foi orientado antes. Se você cair na água, se acontecer algo, deita de costas ou coisa assim. Nada disso."
Coletes também foram alvo de críticas
Além da ausência de instruções, os sobreviventes relataram dificuldades para permanecer na superfície após o barco virar.
Segundo o depoimento, o modelo de colete utilizado prendia apenas na cintura, o que fazia o equipamento subir durante a tentativa de flutuação.
"Havia uma fita que prendia na cintura, mas como não prendia por baixo, entre as pernas, o colete sempre subia."
De acordo com o advogado que acompanha a família, os sobreviventes enfrentaram dificuldades para se manter na superfície porque as correntes do Rio Iguaçu eram fortes.
"Eles tiveram extrema dificuldade de permanecer em cima da água. As correntinhas levavam para baixo e o colete não era suficiente para mantê-los em cima da água", afirmou.
'Não houve explicação sobre o que fazer se o barco virasse': sobreviventes apontam falhas em passeio nas Cataratas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo
Investigação apura possíveis falhas
A Polícia Civil informou que, até o momento, não encontrou indícios de irregularidades na atuação dos dois pilotos da embarcação.
As investigações, porém, passaram a analisar se houve falhas nos protocolos de segurança adotados antes do passeio.
Segundo o delegado responsável pelo caso, os depoimentos indicam que pode ter havido deficiência nas orientações repassadas aos turistas.
"Nós notamos, pelos relatos das testemunhas, uma falta de protocolos de segurança, orientação sobre o que fazer quando a embarcação vira, sobre como colocar o colete e também como verificar se ele está em condições de uso", afirmou.
O laudo da Polícia Científica concluiu que Mark Lessink morreu por afogamento. A investigação agora busca identificar se gestores da operação podem ser responsabilizados por homicídio culposo.
Empresa nega falhas
A empresa responsável pelo passeio informou que realizou, nesta semana, uma reciclagem com todos os funcionários sobre os procedimentos de segurança. Segundo a empresa, as certificações obtidas indicam que não há necessidade de mudanças e, por isso, os protocolos permanecem os mesmos.
A empresa também contestou o relato da família holandesa de que não houve orientações antes do passeio. De acordo com a concessionária, os turistas recebem instruções de segurança em diferentes etapas da experiência.
"Existe um primeiro briefing na carretinha, outro na trilha suspensa e, além disso, toda uma comunicação visual por meio de placas informativas em três idiomas. Antes de iniciar o passeio, é realizado mais um briefing de segurança com orientações específicas sobre a embarcação", informou o gerente administrativo da empresa, Paulo Ricardo de Cordova.
A empresa também rebateu as críticas feitas pelos sobreviventes ao modelo de colete salva-vidas util

deduped_items.title: Por que eleição de Pernambuco virou 'guerra digital' – e o que isso tem a ver com 'virada' da governadora
deduped_items.summary: Governadora Raquel Lyra e ex-prefeito do Recife João Campos trocam acusações sobre 'milícia digital' e máquina de 'fake news'; com popularidade em alta, Lyra reverteu vantagem de Campos nas pesquisas de intenção de voto, embolando eleição.
deduped_items.body_text:
Por que eleição de Pernambuco virou 'guerra digital' – e o que isso tem a ver com 'virada' da governadora
Em uma entrega de equipamentos a policiais de Pernambuco, a governadora Raquel Lyra (PSD) desceu de seu gabinete no Palácio do Campo das Princesas e resolveu correr.
Sem tirar o sapato de salto alto, deu a volta na Praça da República, no centro do Recife, enquanto anunciava para a câmera novos drones, fuzis e viaturas, deixando claro que seu "cardio estava em dia".
O vídeo, do fim do ano passado, acumula mais de 3 milhões de visualizações e 120 mil curtidas no Instagram.
Correr se tornou uma das marcas das redes sociais da governadora, que tenta a reeleição e viu sua popularidade disparar — na internet e nas pesquisas eleitorais — nos últimos meses.
Nos seis primeiros meses do ano, Lyra ganhou proporcionalmente mais seguidores (+18%) no Instagram do que qualquer outro candidato ao governo dos Estados do Nordeste, segundo relatório da AtivaWeb Datalab, empresa de análise de dados focada no monitoramento do comportamento político.
Em 30 dias, entre março e abril, ela chegou a ganhar 76 mil seguidores — são 1,9 milhão hoje ao todo.
São números importantes para as ambições de Lyra em Pernambuco, onde as redes sociais têm se mostrado especialmente um campo de batalha acirrado.
Segundo o mesmo relatório, o Estado concentra 31% do número de seguidores em redes sociais ligadas aos candidatos nas eleições estaduais no Nordeste.
"É o centro da influência política digital nordestina", analisa Alek Maracajá, diretor da empresa, que tem sede na Paraíba.
Contra Lyra, está João Campos (PSB), popular ex-prefeito do Recife reeleito em 2022 com quase 80% dos votos que conquistou seguidores pelo país pelo jeito jovem de engajar nas redes, das dancinhas ao cabelo platinado.
Campos segue como um dos políticos mais populares nas redes no país, sendo o candidato a governo estadual no Nordeste mais seguido no Instagram: são 3 milhões de pessoas.
Mas, enquanto Lyra vem numa crescente, Campos tem enfrentado desafios em um ambiente que ele sempre dominou. Segundo a Ativaweb, o ex-prefeito chegou a ter quedas em suas taxas de engajamento em 2026 — ou seja, a porcentagem de seus seguidores que comentam, curtem ou compartilham seus posts.
Segundo Maracajá, o comparativo técnico indica que Campos domina pelo tamanho e alcance nacional de sua rede, mas Lyra chegou a ter engajamento superior à do ex-prefeito. "João tem o tamanho. Raquel tem o momento", cravou no relatório.
A temperatura digital nas eleições pernambucanas é tão alta que virou rotina a troca de acusações entre os candidatos.
Raquel Lyra tem sido acusada por adversários políticos locais de instrumentalizar uma "milícia digital" contra adversários nas redes sociais.
João Campos disse a jornalistas em junho que "tem sido atacado manhã, tarde e noite por uma verdadeira milícia digital, instrumentalizada de forma inorgânica, com presença de robôs, informações falsas e automatizadas".
"Essa presença que já foi identificada, denunciada e hoje é apurada pela PF em Pernambuco", disse Campos.
A Polícia Federal (PF) não confirmou a abertura da investigação e disse que não comenta apurações em andamento.
A acusação se soma ao caso de um assessor de Lyra flagrado numa lan house num shopping do Recife fazendo uma denúncia anônima contra uma deputada da oposição.
O presidente da Assembleia Legislativa de Pernambuco (Alepe), Álvaro Porto (PSDB), disse na época que o caso mostrava uma "milícia digital" da governadora. O inquérito iniciado na Polícia Legislativa foi posteriormente anulado pela Justiça porque o juiz considerou que não cabia ao órgão investigar os fatos.
Em outro caso, o ministro Gilmar Mendes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou que a PF investigasse um suposto monitoramento ilegal realizado pela Polícia Civil de Pernambuco contra aliados de Campos.
Procurada, a campanha de Lyra não comentou as acusações específicas.
A governadora, por sua vez, também anunciou que recorreria à Justi

deduped_items.summary: Governadora Raquel Lyra e ex-prefeito do Recife João Campos trocam acusações sobre 'milícia digital' e máquina de 'fake news'; com popularidade em alta, Lyra reverteu vantagem de Campos nas pesquisas de intenção de voto, embolando eleição.
deduped_items.body_text:
Por que eleição de Pernambuco virou 'guerra digital' – e o que isso tem a ver com 'virada' da governadora
Em uma entrega de equipamentos a policiais de Pernambuco, a governadora Raquel Lyra (PSD) desceu de seu gabinete no Palácio do Campo das Princesas e resolveu correr.
Sem tirar o sapato de salto alto, deu a volta na Praça da República, no centro do Recife, enquanto anunciava para a câmera novos drones, fuzis e viaturas, deixando claro que seu "cardio estava em dia".
O vídeo, do fim do ano passado, acumula mais de 3 milhões de visualizações e 120 mil curtidas no Instagram.
Correr se tornou uma das marcas das redes sociais da governadora, que tenta a reeleição e viu sua popularidade disparar — na internet e nas pesquisas eleitorais — nos últimos meses.
Nos seis primeiros meses do ano, Lyra ganhou proporcionalmente mais seguidores (+18%) no Instagram do que qualquer outro candidato ao governo dos Estados do Nordeste, segundo relatório da AtivaWeb Datalab, empresa de análise de dados focada no monitoramento do comportamento político.
Em 30 dias, entre março e abril, ela chegou a ganhar 76 mil seguidores — são 1,9 milhão hoje ao todo.
São números importantes para as ambições de Lyra em Pernambuco, onde as redes sociais têm se mostrado especialmente um campo de batalha acirrado.
Segundo o mesmo relatório, o Estado concentra 31% do número de seguidores em redes sociais ligadas aos candidatos nas eleições estaduais no Nordeste.
"É o centro da influência política digital nordestina", analisa Alek Maracajá, diretor da empresa, que tem sede na Paraíba.
Contra Lyra, está João Campos (PSB), popular ex-prefeito do Recife reeleito em 2022 com quase 80% dos votos que conquistou seguidores pelo país pelo jeito jovem de engajar nas redes, das dancinhas ao cabelo platinado.
Campos segue como um dos políticos mais populares nas redes no país, sendo o candidato a governo estadual no Nordeste mais seguido no Instagram: são 3 milhões de pessoas.
Mas, enquanto Lyra vem numa crescente, Campos tem enfrentado desafios em um ambiente que ele sempre dominou. Segundo a Ativaweb, o ex-prefeito chegou a ter quedas em suas taxas de engajamento em 2026 — ou seja, a porcentagem de seus seguidores que comentam, curtem ou compartilham seus posts.
Segundo Maracajá, o comparativo técnico indica que Campos domina pelo tamanho e alcance nacional de sua rede, mas Lyra chegou a ter engajamento superior à do ex-prefeito. "João tem o tamanho. Raquel tem o momento", cravou no relatório.
A temperatura digital nas eleições pernambucanas é tão alta que virou rotina a troca de acusações entre os candidatos.
Raquel Lyra tem sido acusada por adversários políticos locais de instrumentalizar uma "milícia digital" contra adversários nas redes sociais.
João Campos disse a jornalistas em junho que "tem sido atacado manhã, tarde e noite por uma verdadeira milícia digital, instrumentalizada de forma inorgânica, com presença de robôs, informações falsas e automatizadas".
"Essa presença que já foi identificada, denunciada e hoje é apurada pela PF em Pernambuco", disse Campos.
A Polícia Federal (PF) não confirmou a abertura da investigação e disse que não comenta apurações em andamento.
A acusação se soma ao caso de um assessor de Lyra flagrado numa lan house num shopping do Recife fazendo uma denúncia anônima contra uma deputada da oposição.
O presidente da Assembleia Legislativa de Pernambuco (Alepe), Álvaro Porto (PSDB), disse na época que o caso mostrava uma "milícia digital" da governadora. O inquérito iniciado na Polícia Legislativa foi posteriormente anulado pela Justiça porque o juiz considerou que não cabia ao órgão investigar os fatos.
Em outro caso, o ministro Gilmar Mendes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou que a PF investigasse um suposto monitoramento ilegal realizado pela Polícia Civil de Pernambuco contra aliados de Campos.
Procurada, a campanha de Lyra não comentou as acusações específicas.
A governadora, por sua vez, também anunciou que recorreria à Justi

deduped_items.title: Pakistan, Iran reaffirm resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10bn
deduped_items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion, with Commerce Minister Jam calling for transforming “historic brotherly relations” with Iran into a robust economic partnership. deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion, with Commerce Minister Jam calling for transforming “historic brotherly relations” with Iran into a robust economic partnership.
Since March this year, both countries have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures, formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran conflict in the Middle East that has strained economies in the region and beyond.
Their latest engagement took place at the 10th session of the Pak–Iran Joint Trade Committee (JTC), which is being held in Islamabad from August 3-5. The meeting was co‑chaired by Iranian Industry, Mine and Trade Minister Mohammad Atabak and Pakistan’s Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan.
On the occasion, Khan also underscored the urgency to finalise the Pak–Iran Free Trade Agreement, a statement issued by his ministry said.
He called for the removal of barriers in border logistics and cargo movement, highlighting that joint border markets and electronic data interchange could significantly boost trade flows, it added.
According to the statement, both sides reviewed the measures already taken to enhance bilateral commerce at the meeting.
Moreover, the commerce minister said the private sector in both countries was prepared to expand trade, stressing that it was the responsibility of both governments to provide a “predictable and favourable” environment for business to them.
He expressed hope that the JTC meeting would help evolve a practical roadmap to transform trade connectivity and raise the bilateral volume to its maximum potential, the statement said.
For his part, the Iranian minister called Pakistan Iran’s “long‑term strategic trade partner”, the statement said, adding that he expressed Tehran’s desire to expand regional trade and logistics cooperation through Karachi and Gwadar ports, and the optimism that the Pak–Iran FTA would be concluded soon.
Atabak said electricity trade and regional connectivity were “new avenues of economic opportunity” for both countries, according to the statement.
It said Pakistan and Iran “reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, and private sector partnerships”.
Tuesday’s meeting takes place around two weeks after Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni’s visit to Islamabad, where he also held a meeting with Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi. During that meeting, the two sides agreed to expand railway cooperation and strengthen cross-border connectivity.
They also discussed the revival of the Islamabad-Tehran-Istanbul (ITI) freight train service and measures to enhance regional connectivity, the statement said.
As maritime trade faces uncertainty due to the Gulf crisis, Pakistan also permitted exporters in March this year to continue shipping food and pharmaceutical products to Iran via land routes without mandatory banking instruments.
Simultaneously, Islamabad allowed rice exports to Central Asian Republics and Azerbaijan through Iran. In total, 10 food items — including rice, seafood, potatoes, meat, onions, maize, citrus fruits, bananas, tomatoes, and frozen chicken — along with two non‑food items (pharmaceuticals and tents) were cleared for land‑route exports without financial instruments.
To strengthen border management and formalise cross‑border flows, Pakistan established the same month a new customs station at Jeerak in Panjgur district, designated as the fifth crossing point for trade and transit with Iran. The facility aims to regulate passenger movement, document personal baggage, and channel informal trade into the formal economy.
This builds on earlier steps, including the opening of the Kohak Cheedgi crossing in January 2025 and the Gabd Rimdan border point in December 2024.

deduped_items.title: Pakistan to host Iranian officials as Trump’s patience wears thin
deduped_items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan on Monday invited Iran’s parliament speaker and foreign minister for urgent consultations on regional developments, as Tehran described Islamabad as its primary mediator with the US. National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq invited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator with Washington and speaker of parliament. deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Monday invited Iran’s parliament speaker and foreign minister for urgent consultations on regional developments, as Tehran described Islamabad as its primary mediator with the US.
National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq invited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator with Washington and speaker of parliament. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, meanwhile, invited his Iranian counterpart, Seyyed Abbas Araghchi. The invitations were delivered in Tehran late Monday night after Dar spoke with Araghchi.
“They exchanged views on regional and international developments, including the deteriorating situation in Occupied East Jerusalem,” the Foreign Office said in a statement.
It remained unclear when Ghalibaf and Araghchi would travel to Pakistan. A diplomatic source said both men had been asked to come as soon as possible for discussions on regional and international developments. Araghchi was in Iraq on Monday for Arbaeen, which is being observed on Tuesday.
The invitations came roughly 36 hours after US President Donald Trump announced he had canceled imminent strikes against Iran. Trump said allies had urged him to hold off because a deal appeared imminent.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump and persuaded him to call off the planned military action. Trump had also named UAE and Qatar as among the countries that had asked him to cancel the planned strikes.
Iran has been holding talks with Oman about the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian authorities say they are close to an agreement but have not indicated whether the waterway would reopen or remain closed.
Pakistan has been relatively quiet on the mediation front compared with earlier efforts that produced the Islamabad MoU. It has, however, remained engaged through back channels with Iran and, together with Qatar, proposed a ceasefire plan during a nearly 13-day period of escalation.
Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday insisted that Pakistan is the main mediator with US. Spokesman Esmail Baqaei said: “The mediator in the discussions related to Iran and the US is Pakistan, and Qatar also helps in cases where necessary. To say that we have added a new mediator to the existing mediators is not, in the strict sense of the word, the case.”
Meanwhile, President Donald Trump accused Iran’s leadership of being “unbelievably duplicitous” after Tehran denied that any negotiations were underway with the US. The exchange renewed threats from Trump, who warned Iran faced “decapitation” and said he would keep up military pressure until there was a “deal, or total surrender”.
“I think we’re going to maybe get something, but I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Trump said, reiterating his threat to launch a major attack on Iran.
The war of words follows a familiar pattern in the five-month conflict between Washington and Tehran.
The president, who on Sunday said renewed talks would begin “tomorrow afternoon” without naming a venue or participants, added that the US Navy maintains complete control over the Strait of Hormuz.
“Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a deal, or total surrender, is accomplished,” he said.
Trump had told reporters aboard Air Force One that Iran, along with Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, had asked him to hold off on what he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II”.
“Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people,” Trump said on Sunday. He described ongoing discussions as a “last chance for them to sign a good document”.

deduped_items.body_text:
• Washington makes visa bond programme permanent; Bangladesh, Nepal among 50 countries covered, India also excluded
• Visitors from listed nations face refundable deposits of up to $20,000
WASHINGTON: Pakistan is not among the 50 countries whose citizens may now be required to deposit up to $20,000 as a financial guarantee before obtaining a US visitor visa under a new programme that took effect on Aug 1.
The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian countries, Bangladesh and Nepal are covered by the programme, while India is not.
Afghanistan and Iran are not included because the United States does not maintain normal diplomatic relations with either country.
The State Department said the decision followed a review of the 2025 pilot programme, which it said significantly reduced visa overstays among travellers from participating countries and improved compliance with US immigration rules. Officials said those findings prompted Washington to make the programme permanent.
According to the department, there were 45,488 overstays from these 50 countries in 2024. In the first 10 months of the pilot, the number of overstays was fewer than 50. The visa bond requirement has also resulted in a decrease in visa issuance, as some applicants appear to self-select by not paying a bond.
Diplomatic sources also confirmed to Dawn that “Pakistan is not on the list of countries covered by the programme”.
The programme applies to applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas from countries covered by the scheme. Under the new rules, US consular officers may require selected applicants to post a refundable bond of between $10,000 and $20,000 before issuing a visa.
The regulations make permanent a visa bond pilot launched in 2025 after the US State Department concluded that it had helped reduce visa overstays.
The new rules also increase the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 and eliminate the previous $5,000 minimum bond available during the pilot programme.
The 50 countries covered by the programme include 30 African nations as well as countries in Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific.
The bond will be refunded if the visitor complies with all visa conditions and leaves the United States before the authorised period of stay expires. Applicants who overstay or otherwise violate the terms of their visas risk forfeiting the deposit.
The bond requirement does not apply automatically to all applicants from the countries covered by the programme. Instead, US consular officers will determine on a case-by-case basis whether a bond is warranted before issuing a visa.

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion, with Commerce Minister Jam calling for transforming “historic brotherly relations” with Iran into a robust economic partnership.
Since March this year, both countries have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures, formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran conflict in the Middle East that has strained economies in the region and beyond.
Their latest engagement took place at the 10th session of the Pak–Iran Joint Trade Committee (JTC), which is being held in Islamabad from August 3-5. The meeting was co‑chaired by Iranian Industry, Mine and Trade Minister Mohammad Atabak and Pakistan’s Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan.
On the occasion, Khan also underscored the urgency to finalise the Pak–Iran Free Trade Agreement, a statement issued by his ministry said.
He called for the removal of barriers in border logistics and cargo movement, highlighting that joint border markets and electronic data interchange could significantly boost trade flows, it added.
According to the statement, both sides reviewed the measures already taken to enhance bilateral commerce at the meeting.
Moreover, the commerce minister said the private sector in both countries was prepared to expand trade, stressing that it was the responsibility of both governments to provide a “predictable and favourable” environment for business to them.
He expressed hope that the JTC meeting would help evolve a practical roadmap to transform trade connectivity and raise the bilateral volume to its maximum potential, the statement said.
For his part, the Iranian minister called Pakistan Iran’s “long‑term strategic trade partner”, the statement said, adding that he expressed Tehran’s desire to expand regional trade and logistics cooperation through Karachi and Gwadar ports, and the optimism that the Pak–Iran FTA would be concluded soon.
Atabak said electricity trade and regional connectivity were “new avenues of economic opportunity” for both countries, according to the statement.
It said Pakistan and Iran “reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, and private sector partnerships”.
Tuesday’s meeting takes place around two weeks after Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni’s visit to Islamabad, where he also held a meeting with Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi. During that meeting, the two sides agreed to expand railway cooperation and strengthen cross-border connectivity.
They also discussed the revival of the Islamabad-Tehran-Istanbul (ITI) freight train service and measures to enhance regional connectivity, the statement said.
As maritime trade faces uncertainty due to the Gulf crisis, Pakistan also permitted exporters in March this year to continue shipping food and pharmaceutical products to Iran via land routes without mandatory banking instruments.
Simultaneously, Islamabad allowed rice exports to Central Asian Republics and Azerbaijan through Iran. In total, 10 food items — including rice, seafood, potatoes, meat, onions, maize, citrus fruits, bananas, tomatoes, and frozen chicken — along with two non‑food items (pharmaceuticals and tents) were cleared for land‑route exports without financial instruments.
To strengthen border management and formalise cross‑border flows, Pakistan established the same month a new customs station at Jeerak in Panjgur district, designated as the fifth crossing point for trade and transit with Iran. The facility aims to regulate passenger movement, document personal baggage, and channel informal trade into the formal economy.
This builds on earlier steps, including the opening of the Kohak Cheedgi crossing in January 2025 and the Gabd Rimdan border point in December 2024.

deduped_items.summary: Long-haul travelers have long complained about jet lag’s grogginess and irritability. But researchers say the condition goes far deeper than fatigue, disrupting cell repair, altering liver and kidney function, and, in cases of chronic exposure, potentially raising the risk of cancer. deduped_items.body_text:
Long-haul travelers have long complained about jet lag’s grogginess and irritability. But researchers say the condition goes far deeper than fatigue, disrupting cell repair, altering liver and kidney function, and, in cases of chronic exposure, potentially raising the risk of cancer.
A Disrupted Internal Clock
The root cause of jet lag is not simply lost sleep, scientists say, but disruption to the body’s internal clock, which runs on a roughly 24-hour cycle governing when people eat, sleep and stay active.
Under normal conditions, light-sensitive cells in the eye detect darkness and trigger the release of melatonin, the hormone that induces sleep. That process is coordinated by a region of the brain known as the suprachiasmatic nucleus, or SCN.
Russell Foster, a professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford and author of the book “Life Time,” compared the SCN to an orchestra conductor that keeps the body in sync with cycles of night and day. Long-haul flights, he said, throw that system into disarray.
Symptoms tend to worsen with the number of time zones crossed, according to researchers, and are typically more severe on eastbound flights and during shorter winter days.
Airline Crews Face Chronic Exposure
While most travelers experience jet lag only occasionally, airline crews face it as a routine part of their jobs. Research has found that flight attendants working demanding schedules with little rest between flights had higher levels of the stress hormone cortisol than colleagues with lighter workloads.
Elevated cortisol helps the body manage short-term stress, but sustained exposure has been linked to a weakened immune system and increased cardiovascular risk, researchers say.
Brain scans of the flight attendants with heavier schedules also showed smaller right temporal lobes on average, and that group scored lower on memory tests, according to the research.
A separate study at the University of California, Berkeley, simulated jet lag in hamsters over four weeks, mimicking a schedule of transatlantic flights twice weekly. The animals struggled with tasks they normally handled easily, and researchers found they had stopped producing new brain cells in the hippocampus, the region tied to memory. The effects still had not reversed a month later.
Possible Links to Cancer
Laboratory studies have also raised concerns about tumor growth. Mice with induced jet lag showed faster tumor growth, while restoring a normal circadian rhythm slowed tumor development, according to the research. Separate mouse studies found chronic jet lag triggered a progression of liver disease, from fatty liver disease to hepatitis, scarring and eventually liver cancer.
Human data, while observational, points in a similar direction. A study from the 1990s found Canadian pilots had higher-than-average rates of prostate cancer. A more recent meta-analysis found female flight attendants had elevated rates of breast cancer and melanoma, and one survey found flight attendants overall reported higher cancer rates than the general population among women, though not among men.
Researchers caution that the studies are observational and cannot establish that jet lag alone drives the increased risk, since exposure to cosmic radiation during flight and other factors may also play a role.
Steps Travelers Can Take
Health experts recommend several strategies to ease jet lag’s effects:
- Adjust before departure. Travelers heading east should go to bed one to two hours earlier than usual for several days before the flight; those heading west should do the opposite.
- Consider melatonin cautiously. A 2002 Cochrane Review found melatonin can help combat jet lag, though it called for more research into its safety. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention includes melatonin guidance in its travel recommendations, while Britain’s National Health Service does not endorse its use, citing insufficient evidence. deduped_items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran agreed Tuesday to expedite negotiations on a long-awaited free trade agreement, with officials from both countries stressing the need to conclude the pact quickly to boost bilateral trade, according to reports. Officials Reaffirm $10 Billion Trade Target The 10th Pakistan-Iran Joint Trade Committee meeting was held in Islamabad under the joint ... Read more The post Pakistan, Iran agree to fast-track $10 billion free trade agreement talks appeared first on BOL News.
deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran agreed Tuesday to expedite negotiations on a long-awaited free trade agreement, with officials from both countries stressing the need to conclude the pact quickly to boost bilateral trade, according to reports.
Officials Reaffirm $10 Billion Trade Target
The 10th Pakistan-Iran Joint Trade Committee meeting was held in Islamabad under the joint chairmanship of Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan and Iran’s Minister of Industry, Mine and Trade, Mohammad Atabak, according to an official statement issued Tuesday.
The two countries reaffirmed their commitment to raising bilateral trade volume to $10 billion.
Speaking at the meeting, Jam Kamal said the time had come to transform the historic relationship between Pakistan and Iran into a strong economic partnership, and he emphasized the need to finalize the free trade agreement as soon as possible.
He said removing barriers to border logistics, customs and cargo movement was imperative, adding that establishing joint border markets and electronic data interchange systems would significantly increase bilateral trade. He said the private sectors of both countries were ready for trade and that it was the responsibility of the two governments to provide a conducive and reliable business environment.
Jam Kamal said the 10th committee meeting would chart a practical roadmap and elevate economic cooperation between the two countries.
Atabak, for his part, described Pakistan as Iran’s long-term strategic trade partner and expressed a desire to enhance regional trade and logistics cooperation through the ports of Karachi and Gwadar. He also expressed hope that the free trade agreement would be finalized soon and pointed to electricity trade and regional connectivity as new economic opportunities for both countries.
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to further promoting cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity and the private sector. Officials said the meeting reflected the shared commitment of both countries to deepen their economic partnership, enhance regional connectivity and create new opportunities for trade and investment.
Tuesday’s meeting was the 10th session of the Joint Trade Committee since the body was established. The ninth meeting was held in Tehran from Nov. 6-7, 2021.
Pakistan and Iran have maintained a bilateral preferential trade agreement since Sept. 1, 2006. Under that agreement, Pakistan has granted tariff concessions to Iran on 338 tariff lines, while Iran has extended concessions on 309 tariff lines, with average tariff concessions of around 18%. However, due to Iran’s more restrictive tariff regime, duties applied on Pakistani exports remain significantly higher than those imposed on Iranian exports to Pakistan.

deduped_items.title: Iraq tightens security to prevent cross-border attacks amid regional tensions
deduped_items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi authorities have begun implementing tighter security measures to prevent rockets or drones from being launched from Iraqi territory toward neighboring countries, according to a report published […] The post Iraq tightens security to prevent cross-border attacks amid regional tensions appeared first on Iraqi News.
deduped_items.body_text:
Iraq tightens security to prevent cross-border attacks amid regional tensions
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi authorities have begun implementing tighter security measures to prevent rockets or drones from being launched from Iraqi territory toward neighboring countries, according to a report published Tuesday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada, citing security and political sources.
The report said security forces are increasing surveillance in Basra, the deserts of Najaf, Samawa, and Anbar, particularly in areas bordering Saudi Arabia and Jordan.
According to the sources, Iraqi authorities also plan to impose “strict penalties” on any security official found to have allowed attacks to originate from areas under their responsibility.
The reported measures follow an emergency security meeting chaired by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, during which the government announced the formation of a joint security committee tasked with preventing further cross-border attacks.
In a statement issued after the meeting, al-Zaidi instructed security agencies to enforce the law, strengthen stability, and ensure Iraqi territory is not used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries.
Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi also said in a televised interview that the prime minister’s firm position had helped avert what he described as a potential military strike against Iraq.
Despite the new measures, Al-Mada’s sources questioned whether Baghdad would be able to completely prevent future drone launches or avoid possible retaliatory action by neighboring states.
The report said U.S. officials believe some Iran-supplied ballistic missiles remain hidden inside Iraq. However, a senior figure from a major Shiite political party, speaking anonymously, told the newspaper that armed factions have temporarily stepped back from using such missiles following U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to halt what he described as a planned strike against Iran.
According to the report, Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) also ordered the evacuation of facilities in Nineveh as a precaution against potential future U.S. airstrikes.
Al-Mada reported that most members of the ruling Coordination Framework support the government’s official approach to responding to the regional crisis through diplomatic and, if necessary, military channels.
However, the newspaper said one influential Shiite leader continues to oppose the government’s position.
According to the report, armed factions have given the government until Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia following recent military developments, while some groups reportedly oppose Baghdad’s efforts to bring weapons under exclusive state control.
The newspaper also cited political analysts who argued that Iraq remains caught between broader regional tensions involving the United States, Iran, and Gulf countries, increasing the risk of further military escalation.
The claims published by Al-Mada are based on unnamed security and political sources and have not been independently confirmed by Iraqi authorities.

deduped_items.title: PM directs early completion of arrangements as Egypt begins 2027 Hajj preparations
deduped_items.summary: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stressed that all state institutions are working in close coordination to provide the best possible services for Egyptian pilgrims during the upcoming Hajj season, while maintaining close cooperation with Saudi authorities to ensure smooth procedures and facilitate the performance of the pilgrimage rituals. Chairing a meeting of the Higher Hajj Committee … The post PM directs early completion of arrangements as Egypt begins 2027 Hajj preparations appeared first on
deduped_items.body_text:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stressed that all state institutions are working in close coordination to provide the best possible services for Egyptian pilgrims during the upcoming Hajj season, while maintaining close cooperation with Saudi authorities to ensure smooth procedures and facilitate the performance of the pilgrimage rituals.
Chairing a meeting of the Higher Hajj Committee on Monday, August 3, 2026, to discuss regulations for the 1448 AH/2027 Hajj season, Madbouly called for the early completion of all administrative and technical preparations, including travel, accommodation and medical service arrangements.
The meeting was attended by Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir, Social Solidarity Minister Maya Morsy, Civil Aviation Minister Sameh al-Hefny, senior Cabinet and Interior Ministry officials, while the ministers of health, tourism, foreign affairs, Awqaf and labor joined via video conference.
Madbouly said the meeting aimed to ensure effective coordination among all relevant authorities to guarantee full readiness and deliver high-quality services to Egyptian pilgrims.
During the meeting, Assistant Secretary General of the Cabinet Tarek Abdel Razek reviewed an assessment of the 1447 AH Hajj season, including the distribution of Egypt’s pilgrimage visa quota among the authorities concerned.
He highlighted several achievements, including Egypt’s Hajj Affairs Office receiving the Labaytum Silver Award for the first time.
He added that effective coordination between the Egyptian and Saudi authorities ensured that no Egyptian pilgrim remained outside the official Hajj system.
Abdel Razek also noted that a unified database of all Egyptian pilgrims was created through the Hajj Portal.

Clashes in Ethiopia along borders with Sudan, Eritrea stoke worry of larger regional war          
        After four years of a contentious peace between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, fighting broke out between the two sides on Saturday.
The clashes spanned from the Humera border town with Sudan in the north to Shererina in the south and began around midnight, persisting through the afternoon of the next day, three residents in the area told Mada Masr.
The residents said they could hear the sound of mortar shelling and machine gun fire throughout the day, primarily around Shererina.
The clashes began when a force of Tigrayian fighters, who have been stationed in Sudan, crossed into Ethiopia near the village of Legudi outside Humera, according to an Ethiopian military source.
Residents of the border area told Mada Masr that the force, known as “Army 70,” displaced farmers and looted properties belonging to eight agricultural investors, forcing them to flee to urban centers.
The Tigrayan force was quickly engaged by the Ethiopian federal military and pushed back, according to the Ethiopian military source.
Shortly afterward, federal forces launched attacks on TPLF positions in Shererina using heavy artillery and drones, according to the group’s leadership, which described the assault as a direct violation of the Pretoria ceasefire agreement, the 2022 peace deal that ended the two-year civil war in Tigray.
The Ethiopian military has established new checkpoints at main access gates to Humera city, imposing strict security controls and movement restrictions, the Ethiopian military source said. All vehicular and pedestrian movement outside city limits has been prohibited, effectively barring farmers from accessing surrounding agricultural fields.
In southern Tigray, tensions also flared, as eyewitnesses told Mada Masr that a military build-up was visible.
Fearing a broader conflict, hundreds of civilians from surrounding areas fled on foot toward Raya Kobo, quickly overwhelming local hosting capacities and driving further displacement south toward Woldiya and Dessie, Gobeze Aragaw, a resident of Kobo, told Mada Masr.
The clashes are an ominous sign of escalation for a region that has been on the brink of war for months.
While tensions have been steadily escalating between Tigray and the federal government for at least a year following the collapse of the Tigray Interim Administration established under the 2022 agreement, the fighting has a wider resonance.
Ethiopia’s decision to allow the Rapid Support Forces to use its territory as a staging ground for fighting in Sudan’s Blue Nile coupled with its demands for Red Sea access via Eritrea, which has subsequently thrown its weight behind the TPLF, has internationalized the stakes of the Tigray tension. Egypt, adamant in denying Ethiopia Red Sea access, has grown closer to Eritrea, while the United Arab Emirates, a close backer of the RSF and the Ethiopian government, looms in the background.
For now, however, the conflict has largely remained localized.
The TPLF said on Saturday that its forces were acting “in defense of the region” after what it described as government attempts to impose new military realities on the ground. It accused Addis Ababa of failing to implement key provisions of the agreement, including the withdrawal of non-federal forces from Western Tigray and the restoration of civilian administration in the territory.
A former Ethiopian government official who served at the country’s embassy in Khartoum said the federal government holds the TPLF leadership entirely responsible for the collapse of the security arrangements, arguing that the group has spent recent months rebuilding its military structures outside the framework established by the Pretoria agreement.
The Ethiopian military operations are intended to “protect the constitutional order” and prevent the peace deal from collapsing, the former official said. The gove

deduped_items.body_text:
Bakeries voice concerns that new direct debit system could disrupt subsidized bread production          
        A new direct debit system launched by the government at the start of August restructures its financial relationship with mills and bakeries — the supply chain that makes subsidized bread for around 64 million people.
The new system marks the first practical step toward overhauling the workings of Egypt’s largest subsidy program, sources in bakeries across the country told Mada Masr.
The government has said it plans to phase out in-kind bread subsidies, making bread just another option in a range of goods that subsidy program beneficiaries will be entitled to purchase through a monthly cash support program.
The transition has sparked concerns that some of Egypt’s most vulnerable will be left without government-guaranteed access to bread, leaving them exposed to high inflation.
Wheat and flour have always been supplied to mills and bakeries on consignment, with financial accounts settled later.
Under that system, bakeries received payments from the Supply Ministry to cover other production costs such as energy and labor through periodic settlements, without having to purchase flour themselves or provide cash to finance production.
Now, every stage of the bread-making process is set to operate on cash transactions instead. Mills must pay the General Authority for Supply Commodities for wheat up front before receiving it, and bakeries must, likewise, purchase flour from the mills.
The government will then reimburse bakeries only for the amount of bread distributed to subsidy beneficiaries, verifying how much bread they have supplied to consumers through their ration card point-of-sale machines.
Two sources in the General Bakeries Division of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce told Mada Masr the shift to direct debit cannot be separated from the government’s broader plans to overhaul the subsidy system. The move to a financial cycle based entirely on digital payments and bank settlements will allow the state to monitor money and goods moving through the system more closely, they said — one of the key technical requirements for the planned transition to cash support.
The new step begins to shift government support away from the movement of wheat and flour themselves and toward the flow of money instead.
In doing so, it transfers part of the burden of financing daily operations from the state to bakeries, which must now ensure they have enough cash liquidity to pay for flour before recovering their dues from the government.
Supply Minister Sherif Farouk said in a TV interview on Wednesday that the changes will have no impact on citizens. He affirmed that subsidized bread will continue to be priced at 20 piasters per loaf, with each loaf weighing 90 grams, and each beneficiary will continue to be entitled to receive five loaves per day.
He said the new system is intended to strengthen oversight on the movement of wheat and flour, reduce waste and improve the efficiency of subsidy management without affecting beneficiaries’ entitlements.
But many people working in the subsidized bakeries sector said that the new system would turn their operations upside down, adding to already high costs that threaten the viability of their operations.
New cashflow requirements add to existing financial burden on bakeries
The new financial burden posed by the need for extra liquidity is added to rising costs that have already strained bakeries in recent months, bakery owners said to Mada Masr.
Days before the new system took effect, the General Bakeries Division called for their production subsidy to be raised by around 40 percent, arguing that current rates no longer reflect accumulated increases in labor costs, energy prices, operating expenses and administrative fees.

The clashes spanned from the Humera border town with Sudan in the north to Shererina in the south and began around midnight, persisting through the afternoon of the next day, three residents in the area told Mada Masr.
The residents said they could hear the sound of mortar shelling and machine gun fire throughout the day, primarily around Shererina.
The clashes began when a force of Tigrayian fighters, who have been stationed in Sudan, crossed into Ethiopia near the village of Legudi outside Humera, according to an Ethiopian military source.
Residents of the border area told Mada Masr that the force, known as “Army 70,” displaced farmers and looted properties belonging to eight agricultural investors, forcing them to flee to urban centers.
The Tigrayan force was quickly engaged by the Ethiopian federal military and pushed back, according to the Ethiopian military source.
Shortly afterward, federal forces launched attacks on TPLF positions in Shererina using heavy artillery and drones, according to the group’s leadership, which described the assault as a direct violation of the Pretoria ceasefire agreement, the 2022 peace deal that ended the two-year civil war in Tigray.
The Ethiopian military has established new checkpoints at main access gates to Humera city, imposing strict security controls and movement restrictions, the Ethiopian military source said. All vehicular and pedestrian movement outside city limits has been prohibited, effectively barring farmers from accessing surrounding agricultural fields.
In southern Tigray, tensions also flared, as eyewitnesses told Mada Masr that a military build-up was visible.
Fearing a broader conflict, hundreds of civilians from surrounding areas fled on foot toward Raya Kobo, quickly overwhelming local hosting capacities and driving further displacement south toward Woldiya and Dessie, Gobeze Aragaw, a resident of Kobo, told Mada Masr.
The clashes are an ominous sign of escalation for a region that has been on the brink of war for months.
While tensions have been steadily escalating between Tigray and the federal government for at least a year following the collapse of the Tigray Interim Administration established under the 2022 agreement, the fighting has a wider resonance.
Ethiopia’s decision to allow the Rapid Support Forces to use its territory as a staging ground for fighting in Sudan’s Blue Nile coupled with its demands for Red Sea access via Eritrea, which has subsequently thrown its weight behind the TPLF, has internationalized the stakes of the Tigray tension. Egypt, adamant in denying Ethiopia Red Sea access, has grown closer to Eritrea, while the United Arab Emirates, a close backer of the RSF and the Ethiopian government, looms in the background.
For now, however, the conflict has largely remained localized.
The TPLF said on Saturday that its forces were acting “in defense of the region” after what it described as government attempts to impose new military realities on the ground. It accused Addis Ababa of failing to implement key provisions of the agreement, including the withdrawal of non-federal forces from Western Tigray and the restoration of civilian administration in the territory.
A former Ethiopian government official who served at the country’s embassy in Khartoum said the federal government holds the TPLF leadership entirely responsible for the collapse of the security arrangements, arguing that the group has spent recent months rebuilding its military structures outside the framework established by the Pretoria agreement.
The Ethiopian military operations are intended to “protect the constitutional order” and prevent the peace deal from collapsing, the former official said. The gove

deduped_items.title: Chinese investments in Egypt exceed $10bn amid push to deepen economic cooperation
deduped_items.summary: Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said on Monday that Chinese investments in Egypt exceeded $10bn, highlighting growing confidence among Chinese businesses in Egypt’s investment climate as the government reviewed new opportunities to deepen economic cooperation with Beijing. Madbouly made the remarks while chairing the third meeting of the Ministerial Committee for the China Unit, attended […] The post Chinese investments in Egypt exceed $10bn amid push to deepen economic cooperation firs
deduped_items.body_text:
Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said on Monday that Chinese investments in Egypt exceeded $10bn, highlighting growing confidence among Chinese businesses in Egypt’s investment climate as the government reviewed new opportunities to deepen economic cooperation with Beijing.
Madbouly made the remarks while chairing the third meeting of the Ministerial Committee for the China Unit, attended by several ministers and senior government officials, to follow up on the implementation of the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership and explore new areas of cooperation across key economic sectors.
The prime minister said the strategic relationship between Cairo and Beijing continues to deepen under the guidance of the leadership of both countries, building on the progress achieved in recent years to support Egypt’s development agenda and advance shared interests.
He reviewed the latest developments in bilateral cooperation and the progress of several joint projects, stressing the importance of continued coordination among government entities to ensure the effective implementation of the strategic partnership.
Madbouly said Chinese investments in Egypt have now surpassed $10bn, with a large number of Chinese companies operating across a broad range of sectors.
“The figure reflects the growing confidence of the Chinese business community in Egypt’s investment environment and the promising opportunities the country offers to investors,” he said.
According to Cabinet spokesperson Mohamed El-Homsany, the meeting reviewed a pipeline of joint projects and investment opportunities with Chinese partners across several priority sectors, underscoring the breadth of the economic partnership between the two countries.
The discussions covered cooperation in industrial development, seawater desalination, localisation of advanced technologies, telecommunications, transport, mining, clean energy, specialised chemical industries, engineering industries, agriculture, and expanding exports of Egyptian agricultural products.
The proposed projects are expected to support Egypt’s sustainable development agenda by facilitating technology transfer, attracting additional Chinese investment, boosting local manufacturing, and further expanding economic cooperation between the two countries.
Participating ministers also reviewed progress on ongoing Egypt-China projects and discussed additional opportunities to strengthen collaboration across a wide range of strategic sectors, reaffirming both countries’ commitment to deepening their long-standing economic partnership.

deduped_items.title: Syria Interior Ministry Moves to Release Ain Mneen Detainees Amid Protests, Shop Closures and Municipal Resignations
deduped_items.summary: Syrian authorities said Sunday that legal procedures are underway to release individuals detained during recent unrest in the town of Ain Mneen, as residents staged peaceful demonstrations, shuttered shops and local officials resigned in protest over the arrests. The post Syria Interior Ministry Moves to Release Ain Mneen Detainees Amid Protests, Shop Closures and Municipal Resignations first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
deduped_items.body_text:
Syrian authorities said Sunday that legal procedures are underway to release individuals detained during recent unrest in the town of Ain Mneen, as residents staged peaceful demonstrations, shuttered shops and local officials resigned in protest over the arrests.
Protests, Detentions and a Full Municipal Resignation
Tensions rose sharply in Ain Mneen on Sunday as residents held a peaceful sit-in and observed a broad commercial closure. According to local sources and reporting by Enab Baladi, demonstrators demanded the release of all detainees arrested during Friday’s confrontation — including university students, elderly residents, shop owners and local workers — and called for accountability for security personnel accused of assaulting civilians.
In a video circulated online, the town’s mayor announced his resignation, along with the entire municipal council, before a reconciliation committee.
“Residents stand with the state, not against it; they are simply demanding their rights,” he said, adding that municipal leaders would refuse any negotiations until all detainees are freed and those responsible for the assaults are held accountable.
By Sunday afternoon, calm had reportedly returned to Ain Mneen, with discussions underway over possible negotiated solutions.
Interior Ministry Addresses the Arrests
The Rural Damascus Internal Security Command said in a statement carried by state media that the Ministry of Interior recognises the constitutional right to peaceful assembly. Officials said the initial gathering in Ain Mneen two days earlier lacked legal authorization and involved physical attacks on security personnel.
Authorities stressed that arrests were limited to individuals accused of rioting and disturbing public order, and insisted that peaceful demonstrators were not targeted. They added that legal procedures are being finalised to release the detainees once standard undertakings are completed.
Water Dispute Sparked the Confrontation
The unrest began Friday, July 31, when heavy machinery belonging to the regional water authority arrived in the Ba’arjal area near Ain Mneen. Residents attempted to block the equipment, fearing that new drilling operations would drain the local groundwater basin. The confrontation escalated quickly, resulting in injuries and multiple arrests.
The Rural Damascus Media Directorate rejected claims that a new well was being drilled, saying the machinery was deployed solely to conduct maintenance on an existing well to improve drinking-water access. Officials added that community representatives had been briefed on the project beforehand.
Officials Reject Reports of Damascus Market Strike
Separately, Syrian officials denied widespread social-media reports claiming that major commercial markets in central Damascus — including Al-Hamidiyah, Al-Hariqa and Midhat Pasha — had launched a solidarity strike with Ain Mneen.
The head of the Al-Hamidiyah Commercial Market Committee told Syria TV that no general strike had taken place. He said a small number of shop owners briefly closed their stores to attend a solidarity gathering, while images circulating online of shuttered storefronts were taken early in the morning before businesses opened, creating a misleading impression of widespread closures.

Syrian authorities said Sunday that legal procedures are underway to release individuals detained during recent unrest in the town of Ain Mneen, as residents staged peaceful demonstrations, shuttered shops and local officials resigned in protest over the arrests.
Protests, Detentions and a Full Municipal Resignation
Tensions rose sharply in Ain Mneen on Sunday as residents held a peaceful sit-in and observed a broad commercial closure. According to local sources and reporting by Enab Baladi, demonstrators demanded the release of all detainees arrested during Friday’s confrontation — including university students, elderly residents, shop owners and local workers — and called for accountability for security personnel accused of assaulting civilians.
In a video circulated online, the town’s mayor announced his resignation, along with the entire municipal council, before a reconciliation committee.
“Residents stand with the state, not against it; they are simply demanding their rights,” he said, adding that municipal leaders would refuse any negotiations until all detainees are freed and those responsible for the assaults are held accountable.
By Sunday afternoon, calm had reportedly returned to Ain Mneen, with discussions underway over possible negotiated solutions.
Interior Ministry Addresses the Arrests
The Rural Damascus Internal Security Command said in a statement carried by state media that the Ministry of Interior recognises the constitutional right to peaceful assembly. Officials said the initial gathering in Ain Mneen two days earlier lacked legal authorization and involved physical attacks on security personnel.
Authorities stressed that arrests were limited to individuals accused of rioting and disturbing public order, and insisted that peaceful demonstrators were not targeted. They added that legal procedures are being finalised to release the detainees once standard undertakings are completed.
Water Dispute Sparked the Confrontation
The unrest began Friday, July 31, when heavy machinery belonging to the regional water authority arrived in the Ba’arjal area near Ain Mneen. Residents attempted to block the equipment, fearing that new drilling operations would drain the local groundwater basin. The confrontation escalated quickly, resulting in injuries and multiple arrests.
The Rural Damascus Media Directorate rejected claims that a new well was being drilled, saying the machinery was deployed solely to conduct maintenance on an existing well to improve drinking-water access. Officials added that community representatives had been briefed on the project beforehand.
Officials Reject Reports of Damascus Market Strike
Separately, Syrian officials denied widespread social-media reports claiming that major commercial markets in central Damascus — including Al-Hamidiyah, Al-Hariqa and Midhat Pasha — had launched a solidarity strike with Ain Mneen.
The head of the Al-Hamidiyah Commercial Market Committee told Syria TV that no general strike had taken place. He said a small number of shop owners briefly closed their stores to attend a solidarity gathering, while images circulating online of shuttered storefronts were taken early in the morning before businesses opened, creating a misleading impression of widespread closures.
