            Bureau of Labor Funds reports healthy returnsSOLID GAINS: Driven by the AI craze, the funds managed by the bureau, led by the Labor Pension Fund, saw robust returns in the first six months
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 Labor funds administered by the Bureau of Labor Funds reported a return of 28.46 percent in the first half of this year, driven by a boom in the global equity market amid demand for artificial intelligence (AI) products, data released by the bureau showed yesterday. The accumulated gains in the value of assets in the funds’ portfolios and income on investment was about NT$2.2 trillion (US$67.82 billion) from January to June, after these funds posted NT$77.1 billion in gains in June, the bureau said in a statement. As of the end of June, the combined value of the funds the bureau manages — including the Labor Pension Fund, the Labor Retirement Fund, the Labor Insurance Fund and the Employment Insurance Fund — stood at NT$8.896 trillion, bureau data showed. The Bureau of Labor Funds sign is pictured at its office in Taipei in an undated photograph.Photo: Lee Chin-hui, Taipei Times The six-month gains of NT$2.2 trillion translated into a rate of return of 28.46 percent during the January-to-June period, up from 27.7 percent during the January-to-May period, the bureau said. Global equity markets posted initial losses in June amid tensions in the Middle East, which pushed up oil prices, but then geopolitics improved to smooth out market sentiment, the bureau said. Thanks to sound fundamentals, Taiwan’s market continued to receive a boost from strong AI demand, it said. In the first six months of the year, the TAIEX, the Taiwan Stock Exchange’s benchmark index, soared 59.25 percent and the MSCI World Index rose 11.25 percent, while the Bloomberg Barclays Global Aggregate Bond Index dropped 0.21 percent. The bureau said 54.37 percent of its investments were made overseas from January to June, while the remaining 45.63 percent were invested in the domestic market. The labor funds managed by the bureau are mainly aimed at aiding workers. The Labor Pension Fund collects contributions from employers and employees every month and are managed by the bureau to boost asset value to help workers save and invest for retirement. The value of assets in the Labor Pension Fund, launched in 2015, was NT$5.796 trillion as of the end of June, the highest among all labor funds, and its rate of return for the January-to-June period stood at 28.19 percent, the bureau said. The Labor Retirement Fund, which has been in place since 1984, had about NT$1.16 trillion in assets as of the end of June, with a rate of return of 40.74 percent for the six months, it added. Meanwhile, the Bureau of Public Service Pension Fund said yesterday that the Public Service Pension Fund, which the bureau manages, recorded NT$331.08 billion in gains in the first six months of this year, equal to a rate of return of 25.03 percent.

            NPS to begin charging visitors to some national parks
  - By Huang Yi-ching, Wu Liang-yi and Esme Yeh / Staff reporters, with staff writer
 The National Park Service (NPS) is planning to charge visitors to many of the 100 Peaks of Taiwan as early as next year in order to fund environmental conservation and park operations. It has drafted amendments to the National Park Act (國家公園法) to establish a national park fund and charge visitors applying for an entry permit to ecologically protected areas of any of the nine national parks or the Shoushan National Nature Park (壽山國家自然公園). The draft would be sent to the Executive Yuan for review early next year, and could be implemented by the end of next year, sources said. Hikers are pictured in undated photograph.Photo: Wu Liang-yi, Taipei Times The NPS sought the regulatory change after the Control Yuan last year said the Ministry of the Interior should consider charging entry fees, collecting donations and covering facility maintenance costs, based on the “user pays” principle, they added. About 200,000 applications have been received to hike in one of the three alpine national parks — Yushan (玉山), Shei-Pa (雪霸) and Taroko (太魯閣). The draft amendments outline the legal basis and sources of revenue of the national park fund and how it would be spent. Sources of revenue would include government budgets, interest, conservation fees, operating income, fines or forfeits, donations and climate adaptation grants, according to the bill. According to the draft amendments, funds would be on environmental conservation and education, recreation services, international exchanges, volunteer incentives, and other allowances or compensation. Most areas within the three alpine national parks are ecologically protected areas that would charge visitors for entry permits under the pending regulatory change, including 76 of the 100 Peaks of Taiwan, as well as dozens of hiking trails. Entry permits to such protected areas are currently free and receive hundreds of thousands of applications every year, but there is a limit on the daily number of visitors allowed into these areas given the limited environmental carrying capacity. Kenting National Park’s (墾丁國家公園) Longkeng (龍坑) and Nanrenshan (南仁山) and the Yangmingshan National Park’s (陽明山國家公園) Lujiaokeng (鹿角坑) and Huangzuishan (磺嘴山) are ecologically protected areas with many visitors. At present, only a few facilities of national parks, such as parking lots, the Yangming Shuwu (陽明書屋) building, the Oluanpi Park (鵝鑾鼻公園) and the Guangao Lodge (觀高山屋), have fees that flow to the national treasury. Mountain cabins built down the line would also charge fees, such as the one on the Qilai (奇萊) ridgeline within the Taroko National Park, expected to enter service this year. The fees would go to the national park fund if the bill is passed, sources said, adding that the draft stiffens fines and penalties for certain crimes at national parks. For example, burning trees or vegetation would be punishable by imprisonment for up to a year, short-term detention, or a fine of up to NT$1 million. The penalty could be increased by 50 percent if the fire results in a disaster, it added. NPS Deputy Director Chang Wei-chuan (張維銓) said the service has completed the draft but has yet to officially discuss the fee amounts, how to charge them and whether the rates should vary by region. The draft bill was formulated on advice from administrative agencies, civic groups, academics and experts, he said. It would be sent to the ministry for review in October and then sent to the Executive Yuan and the Legislative Yuan for review, he added. National Pingtung University of Science and Technology forestry assistant professor Wu Hsing-ju (吳幸如) said it is not unusual for national parks to charge an entry fee, which Taiwan could have done earlier, in line with international practices. deduped_items.title: Japan proposes tougher income rules for permanent residency
deduped_items.summary: Japan’s immigration agency on Tuesday proposed tougher requirements for granting permanent residency to foreigners, including requiring applicants to maintain income above the average for Japanese households and a certain level of projected pension benefits. The proposed guidelines are part of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s push to create an “orderly society” in which Japanese and foreign nationals coexist while cracking down on illegal activities. The Immigration Services Agency will solicit..
deduped_items.body_text:
Japan proposes tougher income rules for permanent residency
Applicants have to maintain annual household income above the average for Japanese households under the new rules
The Immigration Services Agency will solicit public comments before implementing the new rules from April 2027.
Permanent residents can remain in Japan indefinitely without restrictions on their activities while retaining their original nationality. Applicants generally must have lived in Japan for at least 10 years to qualify.
It differs from naturalisation, through which a person acquires Japanese citizenship.
Under the current guidelines, the three main requirements for obtaining permanent residency are good conduct, sufficient assets or skills to maintain an independent livelihood and that granting permanent residency is in Japan’s best interests.

A student athlete who received more than $110,000 from Alan Jones over a decade has told a Sydney court he reported indecent assaults to police after the broadcaster was arrested in 2024 because he wanted his child to know “right from wrong”.
“I feel like I’m here because of being unable to say no,” the man, known as complainant J, told Downing Centre local court on Tuesday.
The alleged victim, who met Jones when he was 14, said he was “disappointed” in himself for failing to stand up to Jones and the alleged abuse.
“I’m a father now, and I’m a proud father, and I want to teach my [child] right from wrong and what he was doing was wrong,” J said on day two of Jones’s trial on 22 indecent assault and sexual touching charges. Jones has pleaded not guilty.
The complainant, now in his 40s, earlier on Tuesday told the court details of alleged indecent assaults at Jones’s farm in Fitzroy Falls in the Southern Highlands when he was 17.
J said that, after dinner over a glass of wine, Jones told him: “There is only one rule here: There are no rules.”
J told the court that the broadcaster later allegedly said: “Go and have a shower and come out wearing a robe and nothing else.”
Asked by the crown prosecutor Georgina Wright if he followed those instructions, J said: “No, I put my underpants on, and then I put the robe on and went out.” Jones was in a room with a grand piano, the court heard.
Wright asked J: “Why did you put the underpants on?”
“I almost knew what was going to happen,” J replied. “Easy access. He’s going to touch me.”
J alleged Jones was sitting on the lounge, also in a robe, and was drinking a glass of wine.
J alleged that Jones “looked me straight in the eye” and stated in a “quiet”, “calm” and “sympathising tone”: “I said the robe and nothing.”
The alleged victim told the court that Jones then “put his hand back on my penis and started rubbing it”.
Jones has denied all wrongdoing and said the allegations were either baseless or distorted the truth.
Jones’s defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC on Monday argued the alleged victims were egged on to complain by media rivals, and their reliability and credibility were questionable.
This included, Bashir alleged, shockjock Ray Hadley and Sydney Morning Herald columnist Peter FitzSimons.
J on Tuesday told the court that later that same evening in Fitzroy Falls, he and Jones watched TV and discussed sport.
The then-teenager mentioned he was getting tired and said he was going to bed, J told the court.
After J went to his room, he alleged that he heard a “tap, tap, tap”, and Jones came into the room.
“He said ‘Is everything OK [J]?’” J alleged Jones came closer and said in a “really passionate voice … ‘I love you mate’ and pulled me in for a cuddle”.
He alleged that Jones “groped” him on the bum and “it was aggressive”.

“He started to wiggle his body so our penises would cross and touch each other.
“There was a slight opportunity where the grip … was released … I was able to step back and sat on the bed, and said I was going to go to bed.”
J alleged that Jones then walked to the other side of the bed.
“My heart was racing. I was as scared and nervous as I had been in a long time. It was that feeling when you go into a room you’ve never been in, like a scary room, my heart felt like it was going to come out of my chest.
“The defendant placed his hand on my penis and began to squeeze it tight and release it. I was frozen.

“I thought if I do this, and I just do it myself, it can be over … and would prevent him from doing it or being near me or touching me. I thought it was the quickest way to make it over and done with, and that’s what happened.”
J told the court he did not consent to what unfolded in the room.

deduped_items.body_text:
Minns government will not implement recommendation of long-awaited hate speech report
Penry Buckley
The NSW government will not expand a controversial offence for inciting hatred to include religion, sexual orientation or gender identity, against the recommendation of a report which it has been sitting on for eight months.
In a statement this afternoon, the NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, said the government was today releasing the report by former supreme court justice John Sackar, firstprovided to the government in November.
In the report, Sackar has recommended that section 93ZAA of the NSW Crimes Act, an offence for inciting hatred on the grounds of race, brought in last year against the recommendation of the NSW Law Reform Commission, be “amended to included all attributes currently protected by section 93Z”.
Section 93Z, the offence for inciting violence, covers offences committed on the basis of someone’s race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or intersex or HIV/Aids status.
Daley said:
After careful consideration of the Sackar Review and its recommendations, the NSW Government has decided not to expand the existing criminal offence of inciting racial hatred to apply to additional protected attributes.
There is no place for hatred in NSW. Everyone deserves to feel safe, respected and free from intimidation, regardless of their background, faith, sexuality or identity.
The Government’s view is that expanding the racial hatred offence to cover other attributes raises complex questions about freedom of expression, freedom of religion, and the consistent application of the criminal law across the community.”
That’s where we’ll leave our live coverage for the day.
Before we log off, let’s recap the top headlines:
NSW police have arrested and charged two men after one of them allegedly brandished a fake replica gun, wearing a bulletproof vest with a US flag and carrying a toy police badge, at a busy Sydney entertainment precinct.
Top NSW officials urged people to avoid the emergency department except in cases of extreme health needs, warning the next three weeks will see hospitals at capacity amid a surge in winter illness.
Thomas Bradley, aQueensland supreme court judge, will be appointed Queensland’s new governor. Bradley will replace the former state chief health officer Jeannette Young, who has served in the role since 2021.
Betting giant Sportsbetsaid it has no evidence to substantiate allegations made in Monday’s hearing about the Albanese government’s gambling bill, including that gambling companies provided illegal drugs and sex workers to customers.
The new Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, has had his new cabinet sworn in today in what appears to be a major shake-up to portfolios.
Australians lodged nearly 120,000 complaints with the Australian Financial Complaints Authority in the most recent financial year, a record number that reflects the intense economic pressures being felt across the community.
The Australian Medical Association Victoria branch said doctors will engage in a stop-work action on Thursday 13 August, affecting hospitals across the Melbourne CBD and in Parkville. It’s the first time doctors have taken protected industrial action in the area in 20 years.
The chief executive of the Bureau of Meteorology has commissioned an independent review of the agency to “ensure it delivers value to Australians in a rapidly changing environment”.

Penry Buckley
The NSW government will not expand a controversial offence for inciting hatred to include religion, sexual orientation or gender identity, against the recommendation of a report which it has been sitting on for eight months.
In a statement this afternoon, the NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, said the government was today releasing the report by former supreme court justice John Sackar, firstprovided to the government in November.

After careful consideration of the Sackar Review and its recommendations, the NSW Government has decided not to expand the existing criminal offence of inciting racial hatred to apply to additional protected attributes.
There is no place for hatred in NSW. Everyone deserves to feel safe, respected and free from intimidation, regardless of their background, faith, sexuality or identity.
The Government’s view is that expanding the racial hatred offence to cover other attributes raises complex questions about freedom of expression, freedom of religion, and the consistent application of the criminal law across the community.”

deduped_items.title: Editorial: Ceuta: la pinza múltiple
deduped_items.summary: Ha quedado demostrado de diversas maneras que la trágica avalancha de jóvenes marroquíes que la semana pasada ingresaron por decenas de miles a la ciudad española autónoma de Ceuta, enclavada en el norte de África, no constituían un fenómeno migratorio auténtico. Fueron persuadidos por noticias falsas sembradas en redes sociales y grupos de chat de que el ingreso a territorio español había quedado libre; miles de ellos fueron llevados en camiones –y asistidos por policías de su país– hasta la de
deduped_items.body_text:
a quedado demostrado de diversas maneras que la trágica avalancha de jóvenes marroquíes que la semana pasada ingresaron por decenas de miles a la ciudad española autónoma de Ceuta, enclavada en el norte de África, no constituían un fenómeno migratorio auténtico. Fueron persuadidos por noticias falsas sembradas en redes sociales y grupos de chat de que el ingreso a territorio español había quedado libre; miles de ellos fueron llevados en camiones –y asistidos por policías de su país– hasta la demarcación de esa urbe, donde unos superaron las vallas fronterizas y otros se lanzaron al mar para llegar a ella, con un saldo provisional de unos 90 fallecidos.
En suma, fue una acción orquestada desde la monarquía de Marruecos, encabezada por Mohamed VI, el cual utilizó y sacrificó sin escrúpulo alguno a sus propios ciudadanos para poner en jaque y chantajear al gobierno español, como ya lo había hecho en 2021, cuando consiguió, por medio de un operativo semejante, que Madrid legitimara la ocupación marroquí del territorio de la República Árabe Saharaui Democrática (RASD). Ello llevó a su vez a una afectación de las relaciones diplomáticas y comerciales entre España y Argelia, país aliado de la RASD y principal rival estratégico de Marruecos en el Magreb.
Dos diarios informaron ayer que las autoridades españolas detectaron a agentes de los servicios de inteligencia de Rabat entre el alud de extranjeros y apuntaron a Fouad Ali El Himma, consejero y amigo personal de Mohamed VI, como el responsable de organizar y ordenar la incursión de más de 50 mil marroquíes a Ceuta.
Se ha señalado que la principal motivación de la monarquía alauita para emprender esta inescrupulosa y cruenta manipulación masiva era poner en jaque al presidente del gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, quien el pasado 20 de julio realizó una visita a Argel con el propósito de normalizar los vínculos bilaterales, principalmente el abasto de gas argelino a España.
Adicionalmente, no debe olvidarse que Rabat mantiene una estrecha alianza política y estratégica con el régimen israelí y con el gobierno de Donald Trump, los principales inconformes con las posturas críticas de La Moncloa ante el genocidio perpetrado por Tel Aviv en Gaza y ante la injustificada agresión militar que ambos, Estados Unidos e Israel, emprendieron en febrero pasado contra Irán.
Por su parte, las derechas y ultraderechas europeas, si no participaron en instigar la estampida de jóvenes marroquíes sobre Ceuta, al menos aprovecharon muy bien la crisis, empezando por las españolas, las cuales pretendieron azuzar a los sectores xenófobos presentando la incursión masiva de marroquíes en la ciudad autónoma como prueba de la imaginaria aquiescencia del gobierno que encabeza Sánchez ante la supuesta “invasión” de africanos que estaría experimentando España. La primera ministra italiana, Giorgia Meloni, exponente de esas corrientes políticas que lindan con el fascismo, no dudó en exigir una ruptura del ámbito migratorio europeo (espacio Schengen), alegando que Madrid lo había puesto en peligro, pese a que el número de migrantes procedentes de África que se internan a él por Italia casi triplica el de quienes arriban por España.
En suma, los intereses políticos que impulsaron la trágica incursión masiva de marroquíes a Ceuta son tan inocultables como la capacidad de las derechas mundiales para construir una pinza múltiple contra un gobierno europeo que se ha distanciado de las aventuras genocidas de Israel y de Estados Unidos. Y conviene tomar nota de ello.

Fueron persuadidos por noticias falsas sembradas en redes sociales y grupos de chat de que el ingreso a territorio español había quedado libre; miles de ellos fueron llevados en camiones –y asistidos por policías de su país– hasta la demarcación de esa urbe, donde unos superaron las vallas fronterizas y otros se lanzaron al mar para llegar a ella, con un saldo provisional de unos 90 fallecidos.
En suma, fue una acción orquestada desde la monarquía de Marruecos, encabezada por Mohamed VI, el cual utilizó y sacrificó sin escrúpulo alguno a sus propios ciudadanos para poner en jaque y chantajear al gobierno español, como ya lo había hecho en 2021, cuando consiguió, por medio de un operativo semejante, que Madrid legitimara la ocupación marroquí del territorio de la República Árabe Saharaui Democrática (RASD). Ello llevó a su vez a una afectación de las relaciones diplomáticas y comerciales entre España y Argelia, país aliado de la RASD y principal rival estratégico de Marruecos en el Magreb.
Dos diarios informaron ayer que las autoridades españolas detectaron a agentes de los servicios de inteligencia de Rabat entre el alud de extranjeros y apuntaron a Fouad Ali El Himma, consejero y amigo personal de Mohamed VI, como el responsable de organizar y ordenar la incursión de más de 50 mil marroquíes a Ceuta.
Se ha señalado que la principal motivación de la monarquía alauita para emprender esta inescrupulosa y cruenta manipulación masiva era poner en jaque al presidente del gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, quien el pasado 20 de julio realizó una visita a Argel con el propósito de normalizar los vínculos bilaterales, principalmente el abasto de gas argelino a España.
Adicionalmente, no debe olvidarse que Rabat mantiene una estrecha alianza política y estratégica con el régimen israelí y con el gobierno de Donald Trump, los principales inconformes con las posturas críticas de La Moncloa ante el genocidio perpetrado por Tel Aviv en Gaza y ante la injustificada agresión militar que ambos, Estados Unidos e Israel, emprendieron en febrero pasado contra Irán.
Por su parte, las derechas y ultraderechas europeas, si no participaron en instigar la estampida de jóvenes marroquíes sobre Ceuta, al menos aprovecharon muy bien la crisis, empezando por las españolas, las cuales pretendieron azuzar a los sectores xenófobos presentando la incursión masiva de marroquíes en la ciudad autónoma como prueba de la imaginaria aquiescencia del gobierno que encabeza Sánchez ante la supuesta “invasión” de africanos que estaría experimentando España. La primera ministra italiana, Giorgia Meloni, exponente de esas corrientes políticas que lindan con el fascismo, no dudó en exigir una ruptura del ámbito migratorio europeo (espacio Schengen), alegando que Madrid lo había puesto en peligro, pese a que el número de migrantes procedentes de África que se internan a él por Italia casi triplica el de quienes arriban por España.
En suma, los intereses políticos que impulsaron la trágica incursión masiva de marroquíes a Ceuta son tan inocultables como la capacidad de las derechas mundiales para construir una pinza múltiple contra un gobierno europeo que se ha distanciado de las aventuras genocidas de Israel y de Estados Unidos. Y conviene tomar nota de ello.

deduped_items.summary: Hace más de dos mil años, esta tierra vio nacer el confucianismo, que ha influido profundamente en China y el mundo entero. Hace un siglo, esta tierra fue testigo de la lucha gloriosa librada por el ejército y el pueblo en resistencia de la invasión extranjera. Hoy, en esta tierra rebosa el dinamismo de la economía marítima cada vez más integrada con el mundo. Se trata de Shandong, una provincia en la costa oriental de China. deduped_items.summary: Ha quedado demostrado de diversas maneras que la trágica avalancha de jóvenes marroquíes que la semana pasada ingresaron por decenas de miles a la ciudad española autónoma de Ceuta, enclavada en el norte de África, no constituían un fenómeno migratorio auténtico. deduped_items.body_text:
a quedado demostrado de diversas maneras que la trágica avalancha de jóvenes marroquíes que la semana pasada ingresaron por decenas de miles a la ciudad española autónoma de Ceuta, enclavada en el norte de África, no constituían un fenómeno migratorio auténtico. Fueron persuadidos por noticias falsas sembradas en redes sociales y grupos de chat de que el ingreso a territorio español había quedado libre; miles de ellos fueron llevados en camiones –y asistidos por policías de su país– hasta la demarcación de esa urbe, donde unos superaron las vallas fronterizas y otros se lanzaron al mar para llegar a ella, con un saldo provisional de unos 90 fallecidos.
En suma, fue una acción orquestada desde la monarquía de Marruecos, encabezada por Mohamed VI, el cual utilizó y sacrificó sin escrúpulo alguno a sus propios ciudadanos para poner en jaque y chantajear al gobierno español, como ya lo había hecho en 2021, cuando consiguió, por medio de un operativo semejante, que Madrid legitimara la ocupación marroquí del territorio de la República Árabe Saharaui Democrática (RASD). Ello llevó a su vez a una afectación de las relaciones diplomáticas y comerciales entre España y Argelia, país aliado de la RASD y principal rival estratégico de Marruecos en el Magreb.
Dos diarios informaron ayer que las autoridades españolas detectaron a agentes de los servicios de inteligencia de Rabat entre el alud de extranjeros y apuntaron a Fouad Ali El Himma, consejero y amigo personal de Mohamed VI, como el responsable de organizar y ordenar la incursión de más de 50 mil marroquíes a Ceuta.
Se ha señalado que la principal motivación de la monarquía alauita para emprender esta inescrupulosa y cruenta manipulación masiva era poner en jaque al presidente del gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, quien el pasado 20 de julio realizó una visita a Argel con el propósito de normalizar los vínculos bilaterales, principalmente el abasto de gas argelino a España.
Adicionalmente, no debe olvidarse que Rabat mantiene una estrecha alianza política y estratégica con el régimen israelí y con el gobierno de Donald Trump, los principales inconformes con las posturas críticas de La Moncloa ante el genocidio perpetrado por Tel Aviv en Gaza y ante la injustificada agresión militar que ambos, Estados Unidos e Israel, emprendieron en febrero pasado contra Irán.
Por su parte, las derechas y ultraderechas europeas, si no participaron en instigar la estampida de jóvenes marroquíes sobre Ceuta, al menos aprovecharon muy bien la crisis, empezando por las españolas, las cuales pretendieron azuzar a los sectores xenófobos presentando la incursión masiva de marroquíes en la ciudad autónoma como prueba de la imaginaria aquiescencia del gobierno que encabeza Sánchez ante la supuesta “invasión” de africanos que estaría experimentando España. La primera ministra italiana, Giorgia Meloni, exponente de esas corrientes políticas que lindan con el fascismo, no dudó en exigir una ruptura del ámbito migratorio europeo (espacio Schengen), alegando que Madrid lo había puesto en peligro, pese a que el número de migrantes procedentes de África que se internan a él por Italia casi triplica el de quienes arriban por España.
En suma, los intereses políticos que impulsaron la trágica incursión masiva de marroquíes a Ceuta son tan inocultables como la capacidad de las derechas mundiales para construir una pinza múltiple contra un gobierno europeo que se ha distanciado de las aventuras genocidas de Israel y de Estados Unidos. Y conviene tomar nota de ello.

deduped_items.title: Una explosión de una pipa dejó cuatro muertos en Tlaquepaque: ¿Qué provocó el incidente?
deduped_items.summary: La explosión de una pipa cargada con chapopote dentro de una pensión de vehículos en San Pedro Tlaquepaque, Jalisco, deja saldo de cuatro personas fallecidas, presuntamente empleadas del establecimiento.Los hechos ocurrieron en la colonia Las Huertas, en la confluencia de las calles Tamiahua y Pitayos, donde se incendió una pipa cargada con 58 mil litros de chapopote, y los trabajadores del lugar realizaros trabajos para contener el fuego, y entonces sobrevino un fuerte estallido.Personal de cue

deduped_items.summary: La explosión de una pipa cargada con chapopote dentro de una pensión de vehículos en San Pedro Tlaquepaque, Jalisco, deja saldo de cuatro personas fallecidas, presuntamente empleadas del establecimiento.Los hechos ocurrieron en la colonia Las Huertas, en la confluencia de las calles Tamiahua y Pitayos, donde se incendió una pipa cargada con 58 mil litros de chapopote, y los trabajadores del lugar realizaros trabajos para contener el fuego, y entonces sobrevino un fuerte estallido.Personal de cue

deduped_items.title: Nazarena Vélez y el presente que soñó después de tanto dolor: "Me fui haciendo a los ponchazos"
deduped_items.summary: Tras una vida marcada por la exposición, pérdidas y escándalos frente a las cámaras, la actriz vive su etapa de mayor plenitud.En diálogo con Clarín, repasó su historia y habló de su presente como mamá, abuela y pareja.Además, reflexionó sobre su rol en LAM y en stream, y contó cómo vive el regreso al teatro con Un cambio inesperado.
deduped_items.body_text:
A los 14 años, Nazarena Vélez dio sus primeros pasos en el mundo del espectáculo y, desde entonces, su vida transcurrió prácticamente delante de las cámaras.
El público la vio alcanzar grandes éxitos en la televisión y el teatro, pero también atravesar algunos de los momentos más dolorosos de su historia personal: pérdidas irreparables, polémicas separaciones, escándalos, conflictos familiares y desafíos que siempre enfrentó bajo la mirada de los medios y del público.
Hoy, a los 52 años, la actriz asegura estar atravesando uno de los momentos más plenos de su vida.
En pareja desde hace más de siete años con Santiago "Bocha" Caamaño, disfrutando de su rol de mamá y abuela, y combinando su trabajo como panelista de LAM (América), conductora de Storytime (Bondi live) y productora teatral, Nazarena encontró un equilibrio que durante mucho tiempo pareció esquivo.

Donald Trump es solo superado por Nixon en impopularidad: las encuestas que encienden las alarmas para el presidente de EE. UU. y los republicanos
A poco más de dos meses de las elecciones legislativas de noviembre, el republicano tiene un respaldo entre el 32 y el 34 por ciento, un desplome.
Solo Richard Nixon, en los días previos a su renuncia por el escándalo de Watergate, registraba niveles de aprobación más bajos que los de Donald Trump a esta altura de su segundo mandato presidencial.
A poco más de dos meses de las elecciones legislativas de noviembre, una serie de encuestas divulgadas en los últimos días ubican al presidente de Estados Unidos con un respaldo de apenas entre el 32 y el 34 por ciento, un desplome que ha encendido las alarmas entre los republicanos ante el riesgo de perder el control del Congreso.
Las cifras provienen de tres de los sondeos nacionales más recientes.
Quinnipiac encontró que solo el 32 por ciento de los votantes aprueba la gestión de Trump, frente al 58 por ciento que la desaprueba. CNN situó su aprobación en el 34 por ciento y AP-NORC en el 33 por ciento, registros que se encuentran entre los más bajos de toda su carrera política y, en los tres casos, reflejan un deterioro frente a mediciones anteriores.
Sin embargo, lo que convierte esos datos en algo especialmente significativo es la comparación histórica.

deduped_items.title: Venezuela’s New “Institutional Dialogue” Had a Wobbly Start
deduped_items.summary: Much-anticipated talks kicked off with an alleged phone call and matching statements, which the US welcomed
deduped_items.body_text:
Venezuela’s New “Institutional Dialogue” Had a Wobbly Start
Much-anticipated talks kicked off with an alleged phone call and matching statements, which the US welcomed
Y así arrancó.
August 1 arrived with no sign the talks would begin, nor confirmation about those involved in each delegation. Mauricio Claver-Carone, the Americans’ informal intermediary coordinating the talks, announced his departure from the famous “Viceroy” role the day before, though several sources claim he was pushed out. The uncertainty just increased until radio silence broke, when Dinorah Figuera and Jorge Rodríguez published their respective statements at around 6 pm Caracas time, via X.
Both of them claimed to have held a phone call “to commence” the so-called dialogue process between the Rodríguez administration, under the Trump administration’s tutelage, and an opposition group also under the Trump administration’s tutelage. This looks nothing like the start of previous talks featuring chavismo and the opposition, with pictures of mediators and negotiators in a meeting hosted by some Caribbean nation.
We can imagine that, as nothing was really prepared for last weekend, Rodríguez and Figuera simply rang each other on WhatsApp and agreed what they would put in writing to leave a public record that the thing had begun. That’s if the call actually happened.
All statements established the same three-point agenda: the earthquake response (surely a subject Rodríguez is invoking to postpone anything that is not reconstruction), the strengthening of democracy (which has a different meaning for each stakeholder), and political rights and guarantees (what Venezuelans are demanding, in third place).
Rodríguez skipped any mention of a transition, or the United States, or the chavista National Assembly.
Shortly after, a State Department official called Dylan Johnson said the “US welcomes this announcement.” Today’s press statement by State echoes the agenda points shared by Figuera and Rodríguez.
When both camps confirmed the start date on July 14, the response to the disaster did not appear as an agenda point for the Figuera-led delegation. It seems Jorge Rodríguez managed to sneak it in with the gringos’ approval.
Rodríguez addressed Figuera as the “representative of a sector of the Venezuelan opposition” and skipped any mentions of a transition, or the United States. His statement did not mention the chavista National Assembly or display its logo either. Instead, he spoke of a national government delegation where he stands out as coordinador and includes six members. Second in the list is Ana María Sanjuan, a close advisor of the Rodríguez siblings who joined the government as minister of education in March. Then there is Jorge Arreaza (one of the most senior chavista figures in the current legislature and a usual suspect in prominent commissions), Pedro Infante (the parliament’s vice president), and two PSUV lawmakers strongly linked to the ruling party’s youths: América Pérez and Génesis Garvett. The latter is a chavista politician-influencer born in 1999.
Machado said disagreements with the Trump administration concern the speed and urgency of the transition, and demanded short-term results.
Figuera said the first in-person meeting is set to take place next week in Caracas. She confirmed the US-backed opposition delegation is composed of a political technical commission of six members (Marco Aurelio Quiñones, Ramón López, Jorge Millán, Juan Miguel Matheus, and Sergio Vergara and herself) and a supporting commission (Macario González, Julio César Moreno, Desiree Barboza and Elimar Díaz). Figuera thanked the US and Marco Rubio for their backing of the transition before signing off on behalf of the 2015 National Assembly, which doesn’t actually exist anymore.
In an August 2 interview, María Corina Machado restated what she and Edmundo González had already established: she will not join the talks nor block them. Venevisión aired 15 minutes of the conversation

deduped_items.title: African politics and the widening distance between power and consequence
deduped_items.summary: The African Union’s decision not to intervene in Burundi’s 2016 crisis reveals a deeper pattern in continental politics: authority is often furthest from consequence, while responsibility falls on those with the least power. From Burundi to contemporary debates on migration and xenophobia, leadership emerges less as a question of rhetoric than of who is expected to carry the costs of political failure.

deduped_items.title: Ethiopia: Two Presidents, No Government - Why Tigray's War Is Coming Back
deduped_items.summary: [African Arguments] In Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia's northern Tigray region, two men call themselves president. Ce dernier désigne le « génocide pour des gains économiques », c'est-à-dire le coût humain et social des conflits liés à l’exploitation des ressources naturelles. Cette journée de commémoration rend hommage aux victimes de ces violences de masse. Au-delà des cérémonies, le gouvernement a surtout clarifié la manière dont il entend désormais défendre ce dossier sur la scène internationale. Les autorités congolaises ont clarifi

deduped_items.title: Israel is not 'testing' its ceasefires. It's violating them
deduped_items.summary: Israel is not 'testing' its ceasefires. It's violating them Submitted by Barry Malone on Mon, 08/03/2026 - 15:45 As the Israeli military ignores deals in Gaza and Lebanon and continues its industrial-scale killing, the western media turns a blind eye A mourner carries the shrouded body of an infant killed in an overnight Israeli air strike at al-Shifa Hospital, in Gaza City, on 2 August 2026 (Omar al-Qattaa/AFP) On How many people do you need to kill before you’ve violated a ceasefire? One, sure
deduped_items.body_text:
Israel is not 'testing' its ceasefires. It's violating them
How many people do you need to kill before you’ve violated a ceasefire?
One, surely. But what about two? 10? 100?
Or how about more than 1,200? That’s how many Palestinians Israel has killed in Gaza since agreeing to an ostensible ceasefire with Hamas in October.
Israel has also continued to pummel southern Lebanon, despite a “ceasefire” there. But the western media appears to see no violations at all. Instead, it sees ceasefires that are “fragile”, “tested”, “strained” or “shaky”.
Given that news reporting is supposed to rely on precision and accuracy, you’d imagine organisations such as the BBC, Reuters, the Associated Press and CNN have read the terms of the deal that was signed between Israel and Hamas in Egypt. It’s unequivocal, and there really isn’t much room for interpretation.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
There were conditions that needed to be fulfilled within the first 72 hours before the truce could take effect, including the withdrawal of Israeli forces to agreed lines within Gaza, and the return by Hamas of all remaining Israeli hostages, living or dead.
Once the prerequisites were met, which they were, the text said that “all military operations, including aerial and artillery bombardment and targeting operations will be suspended”.
Snuffed out
It’s worth pausing on those words: “all military operations, including aerial and artillery bombardment and targeting operations will be suspended”.
Now square that with more than 1,000 dead Palestinians. Square it with the fact that many were women and children. Square it with the Israeli attack on southern Lebanon that killed school principal Esperanza Ghandour, her mother, a domestic worker and a Syrian labourer as they travelled together in a car.
Square it with the eight people killed at a Palestinian funeral last month. And dare try to square it with the Israeli attack on Gaza that killed Firas al-Masri; his wife, Salsabeel; and their three daughters and son.
None of these firmly established truths seem to stop international journalists from abandoning their duty to call things what they are
They were snuffed out by an occupying force as they slept in their family home, a place that is supposed to be one of love, safety and security.
I could not find a single report in the western media that described the massacre of the Masri household as a ceasefire violation. That’s a pattern across similar atrocities.
Israel said it was targeting a Hamas member without, as usual, providing evidence. But let’s assume for illustrative purposes that Firas al-Masri was in Hamas. After all, since the bogus October agreement, whenever Israel claims it has killed a Hamas member, the western media seems fine with it.
But who did Israel agree the ceasefire with? Yes, Hamas.
None of these firmly established truths seem to stop international journalists from abandoning their duty to call things what they are.
Double standards
A Reuters report on the targeted killing of the Masri family captured some of the horror, and quoted Masri’s father as he mourned the loss of his son, his daughter-in-law, his grandson and three granddaughters.
But despite that, the news agency managed to write 500 words - which also catalogued five other Israeli attacks on Gaza in the preceding days - without coming even close to saying that Israel had violated the ceasefire.
Instead, Reuters treated the truce as an existing reality, not a fiction that is ignored on a daily basis, using this remarkable sentence construction: “The latest deaths add to a toll of more than 1,160 Palestinians, mostly civilians, killed by Israeli attacks since an October ceasefire between Israel and Hamas militants took effect.”
“Since” the ceasefire took effect.
It says a lot about the difference in how the international media reports on Israel, and

deduped_items.title: هل أخذت قضية الصحافية الروسية في فرنسا أبعادا دولية؟
deduped_items.summary: تسارعت الأحداث بخصوص وجود الصحافية الروسية كسينيا فيدوروفا على التراب الفرنسي منذ أن صدر في حقها قرار يقضي بترحيلها وتعليق أصولها المالية للاشتباه في اضطلاعها بدور إعلامي تضليلي استجابة لأجندة روسية بحسب الادعاءات الحكومية الفرنسية. وعلى الرغم من الاستئناف الذي تقدمت به، إلا أن محكمة في باريس رفضت الإثنين هذا الطلب. فهل أصبحت قضية المديرة السابقة لقناة "روسيا اليوم" قضية دولة؟ وهل تعامل باريس مع هذه الصحافية يتضمن فعلا مساسا بحرية التعبير؟

deduped_items.summary: تسارعت الأحداث بخصوص وجود الصحافية الروسية كسينيا فيدوروفا على التراب الفرنسي منذ أن صدر في حقها قرار يقضي بترحيلها وتعليق أصولها المالية للاشتباه في اضطلاعها بدور إعلامي تضليلي استجابة لأجندة روسية بحسب الادعاءات الحكومية الفرنسية. وعلى الرغم من الاستئناف الذي تقدمت به، إلا أن محكمة في باريس رفضت الإثنين هذا الطلب. فهل أصبحت قضية المديرة السابقة لقناة "روسيا اليوم" قضية دولة؟ وهل تعامل باريس مع هذه الصحافية يتضمن فعلا مساسا بحرية التعبير؟

deduped_items.normalised_title: هل أخذت قضية الصحافية الروسية في فرنسا أبعادا دولية؟

deduped_items.title: Mozambique: "Let us be men and women of reconciliation and peace to build peace"
deduped_items.summary: This is the deep conviction of Sisters Maria do Céu and Amélia Alexandre, Mozambican religious missionaries of the Congregation of the Precious Blood, who, in a recent interview with Vatican News, spoke about ongoing religious formation and the professional training for religious women. The two sisters also had a message for Mozambicans urging their compatriots not to give up in the face of difficulties. They called upon Mozambicans, especially young people, to embrace peace and reconciliation R
